candidates.title: General Provisions (40 CFR part 63, subpart A)

gates.question: Does the applicable subpart require you to comply with the General Provisions in 40 CFR part 63, subpart A?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart A requirements are invoked for the affected source; no -> Subpart A requirements are not invoked by that subpart
gates.quote: If you own or operate a new affected source, you must comply with the requirements of the General Provisions in 40 CFR part 63, subpart A as specified in Table 1 to this subpart.

missing: Table 1 to the subpart showing which General Provisions from Subpart A apply

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Secondary Copper Smelters

gates.question: Does your facility meet the definition of a 'secondary copper smelter' in this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> the facility may be within the industry category covered by this subpart; no -> the facility is not in that industry category
gates.quote: Secondary copper smelter means a facility that processes copper scrap in a blast furnace and converter or that uses another pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper from copper scrap, including low-grade copper scrap.

gates.question: Does your operation use a smelting furnace, melting furnace, or other vessel that contains molten material (and capture and control its exhaust)?
gates.test: yes -> the equipment-level affected source requirement in this subpart is relevant; no -> this equipment-level requirement is not relevant
gates.quote: For each smelting furnace, melting furnace, or other vessel that contains molten material, you must install and operate a capture system that collects the gases and fumes from the vessel

gates.question: Is the secondary copper smelter an area source of HAP emissions?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart's area-source standards are the relevant NESHAP; no -> this subpart does not apply on the basis of area-source status
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a new secondary copper smelter that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions.

gates.question: Was construction or reconstruction of the affected secondary copper smelter commenced on or after October 6, 2006 (i.e., is it a 'new affected source')?
gates.test: yes -> the source is a new affected source for this subpart; no -> the source is not a 'new affected source' under this subpart
gates.quote: Your secondary copper smelter is a new affected source if you commenced constructed or reconstruction of the affected source on or after October 6, 2006.

gates.question: If this is a new affected source, did startup occur after January 23, 2007?
gates.test: yes -> compliance with this subpart is required upon startup; no -> compliance date was January 23, 2007
gates.quote: If you startup a new affected source after January 23, 2007, you must achieve compliance with the applicable provisions of this subpart upon startup of your affected source.

missing: Date construction/startup or reconstruction to determine new vs existing (post-October 6, 2006)
Confirmation that the facility produces anode copper via a pyrometallurgical purification process (versus merely melting scrap to ingots or simple shapes)
Whether the facility has been designated an area source by the permitting authority (the scenario states synthetic minor but documentary confirmation may be needed)

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Aluminum, Copper, and Other Nonferrous Foundries

gates.question: Does your facility meet the definition of a 'copper foundry' that melts copper and pours molten copper into molds to manufacture complex castings?
gates.test: yes -> the facility falls within the copper foundry category potentially subject to this subpart; no -> the facility is not a copper foundry under this subpart
gates.quote: Copper foundry means a facility that melts copper and pours molten copper into molds to manufacture copper or copper-based alloy castings (excluding die casting) that are complex shapes.

gates.question: Does your operation pour molten copper into molds to make complex shape castings (rather than casting simple shapes like anode copper, sows, ingots, billets, bars, or copper cake)?
gates.test: yes -> the foundry equipment-level affected source definition applies; no -> the operation may be excluded from this subpart as a primary/secondary metal producer producing simple shapes
gates.quote: For purposes of this subpart, this definition does not include primary or secondary metal producers that cast molten copper to produce simple shapes such as sows, ingots, billets, bars, anode copper, or copper cake.

gates.question: Is your facility an aluminum, copper, or other nonferrous foundry as described in the applicability provision?
gates.test: yes -> the applicability criteria in this subpart must be evaluated; no -> the subpart does not apply on the basis of foundry category
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an aluminum foundry, copper foundry, or other nonferrous foundry as defined in § 63.11556, “What definitions apply to this subpart?”

missing: Annual metal melt production or capacity (to determine if the foundry meets the 600 tpy threshold) and whether this is a new or existing affected source relative to February 9, 2009
Whether the facility pours molten copper into molds to produce complex castings versus producing anode copper or other simple shapes

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Secondary Nonferrous Metals Processing Facilities

gates.question: Is your facility a 'secondary nonferrous metals processing facility' as defined in 40 CFR 63.11472?
gates.test: yes -> the facility may be in the industry category covered by this subpart; no -> this subpart does not apply on the basis of that industry category
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a secondary nonferrous metals processing facility (as defined in § 63.11472) that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions.

missing: Text of the definition in 40 CFR 63.11472 (what operations/equipment constitute a 'secondary nonferrous metals processing facility')
Details tying the plant's specific processes (tilting anode furnace, fluxes, oxidation/reduction, casting anodes) to the definition in § 63.11472

checklist.item: Does the facility melt copper scrap and cast product into anode copper (anodes for electrolytic refining) using a pyrometallurgical process (tilting anode furnace with flux, oxidation/reduction, and casting to anodes)?
Does the facility pour molten copper into molds to manufacture complex shape castings (rather than producing simple shapes like anode copper, sows, ingots, billets, bars, or copper cake)?

candidates.title: National Perchloroethylene Air Emission Standards for Dry Cleaning Facilities

gates.question: Does your facility use perchloroethylene (PCE) in dry cleaning?
gates.test: yes -> proceed to next gates; no -> Subpart M does not apply to you
gates.quote: Applicability. (a) The provisions of this subpart apply to the owner or operator of each dry cleaning facility that uses perchloroethylene.

gates.question: Is the dry cleaning system located in a building with a residence (including a residence that is vacant)?
gates.test: yes -> building-with-residence requirements may apply; no -> those building-with-residence requirements do not apply
gates.quote: If they are located in a building with a residence(s), even if the residence is vacant at the time of this notification;

gates.question: Does the facility emit or have the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons/year) of PCE?
gates.test: yes -> facility is a major source (major-source requirements apply); no -> facility is an area source (area-source requirements apply)
gates.quote: A dry cleaning facility is a major source if the facility emits or has the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons per year) of perchloroethylene to the atmosphere.

gates.question: Is your total yearly PCE consumption below the exemption thresholds (for example less than 530 liters (140 gallons) per year)?
gates.test: yes -> certain exemptions in §63.320(d)/(e) may apply; no -> those exemptions do not apply and full requirements apply
gates.quote: if the total PCE consumption of the dry cleaning facility is less than 530 liters (140 gallons) per year. Consumption is determined according to § 63.323(d).

gates.question: Is the dry cleaning system located in a building with a residence after December 21, 2020?
gates.test: yes -> after Dec 21, 2020 the owner/operator must eliminate any emission of PCE from such a dry cleaning system; no -> the Dec 21, 2020 building-with-residence prohibition does not apply
gates.quote: After December 21, 2020, the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of PCE from any dry cleaning system that is located in a building with a residence.

missing: Current yearly perchloroethylene (PCE) consumption (volume and 12-month sum)
Whether the dry cleaning system actually uses perchloroethylene (PCE)
Whether the dry cleaning machine is coin-operated
Date the dry cleaning system commenced construction or reconstruction (to determine new/existing status)
Whether the dry cleaning system is located in a building with a residence (confirm physical fact; user reports apartment above but confirm)

candidates.title: General Provisions (compliance and maintenance)

gates.question: Is your dry cleaning system an affected source for which a relevant standard under section 112 of the Act has been established?
gates.test: yes -> General Provisions in §63.6 apply to owner/operators of affected sources; no -> §63.6 does not apply as an affected-source provision
gates.quote: The requirements in this section apply to the owner or operator of affected sources for which any relevant standard has been established pursuant to section 112 of the Act

gates.question: If your source is an existing affected source, has it complied by the compliance date established in the applicable subpart?
gates.test: yes -> source should already be complying by that subpart's compliance date; no -> the source must comply by the compliance date established in the applicable subpart
gates.quote: the owner or operator of an existing source shall comply with such standard by the compliance date established by the Administrator in the applicable subpart(s) of this part.

missing: Whether the dry cleaning system is an "affected source" under a section 112 standard (e.g., confirmation that Subpart M applies)
The compliance date specified in the applicable subpart for this source (determined from Subpart M provisions)

candidates.title: (Sample language from Subpart EEEE included in provided sections)

gates.question: Do you operate equipment identified in § 63.2338(b)(1) through (5) that would bring your operations under Subpart EEEE?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart EEEE requirements may apply to the equipment; no -> Subpart EEEE does not apply to your equipment
gates.quote: You must be in compliance with the emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards in this subpart at all times when the equipment identified in § 63.2338(b)(1) through (5) is in OLD operation.

gates.question: Are you required to operate and maintain any affected source consistent with § 63.6(e)(1)(i) under this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> you must operate and maintain sources according to § 63.6(e)(1)(i); no -> that particular duty may not apply
gates.quote: Except as specified in paragraph (d) of this section, you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).

missing: Whether you operate the specific equipment listed in § 63.2338(b)(1)-(5) (the equipment that triggers Subpart EEEE applicability)
Whether Subpart EEEE overlaps any activities at your facility (most likely not for a perchloroethylene dry cleaner)

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Source NESHAP

gates.question: Is the facility primarily engaged (>=50% production) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)-(9)?
gates.test: yes -> facility falls within a listed metal fabrication/finishing source category (proceed to affected_source); no -> this subpart's source-category criterion not met
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in the operations in one of the nine source categories listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (9) of this section.

gates.question: Does the facility perform any listed metal fabrication/finishing operations (e.g., machining, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding/polishing with machines, spray painting, welding) using materials that contain or have the potential to emit MFHAP?
gates.test: yes -> one or more affected-source categories present (subject to subpart if other gates met); no -> that affected-source category is not present (other categories may still apply)
gates.quote: A machining affected source is the collection of all equipment and activities necessary to perform machining operations which use materials that contain MFHAP

gates.question: Do materials used at the facility contain MFHAP at or above the concentration thresholds (>=0.1% by weight for cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel; >=1.0% by weight for manganese)?
gates.test: yes -> materials are considered to contain MFHAP (affected-source requirements apply to operations using them); no -> operations using those materials are not subject for MFHAP control
gates.quote: Materials that contain MFHAP are defined to be materials that contain greater than 0.1 percent for carcinogens, as defined by OSHA at 29 CFR 1910.1200(d)(4), and greater than 1.0 percent for noncarcinogens.

gates.question: Is the facility a research or laboratory facility (or otherwise explicitly exempt under §63.11514(e)-(h))?
gates.test: yes -> exempt from this subpart; no -> exemption does not apply
gates.quote: This subpart does not apply to research or laboratory facilities, as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act (CAA).

gates.question: Are the operations limited to tool/equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in §63.11522?
gates.test: yes -> those activities are excluded from this subpart; no -> activities are not excluded
gates.quote: This subpart does not apply to tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in § 63.11522,

gates.question: Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced before April 3, 2008 (existing) or on/after April 3, 2008 (new)?
gates.test: yes (commenced before April 3, 2008) -> affected source is existing; no (commenced on/after April 3, 2008) -> affected source is new
gates.quote: An affected source is existing if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source, as defined in § 63.2, "General Provisions" to part 63, before April 3, 2008.

gates.question: If the facility is an affected source, has it met the compliance dates for existing or new sources?
gates.test: yes -> compliance date requirements satisfied; no -> compliance deadline, implementation required
gates.quote: If you own or operate an existing affected source, you must achieve compliance with the applicable provisions in this subpart by July 25, 2011.

missing: Table 1 descriptions that define the nine source categories (to confirm whether SIC/NAICS and product types map to one of the nine categories)
Specific information on which metal fabrication/finishing operations are performed at the plant (machining, welding, spray painting, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding/polishing with machines)
Material composition data (MSDS or formulation data) for substrates, paints, welding rods, abrasives to determine whether MFHAP thresholds are met for each operation
Facility-level emissions or permitting information to confirm area vs. major source status for Subpart XXXXXX (numeric major-source thresholds are not provided in the supplied XXXXXX text)
Whether the site is a military installation or performs military-munitions manufacturing (exemptions in §63.11514(g)-(h))

candidates.title: Plating and Polishing Area Source NESHAP

gates.question: Is the facility a plating and polishing facility (engaged in electroplating, electroless plating, thermal spraying, dry mechanical polishing, electroforming, or electropolishing)?
gates.test: yes -> facility is the plating/polishing source category (proceed to affected_source and threshold gates); no -> this subpart likely not applicable
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a plating and polishing facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions and meets the criteria specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section.

gates.question: Does the plant operate any of the listed affected units: tanks used for non-chromium electroplating/electroforming/electropolishing/electroless plating, thermal spraying operations, or dry mechanical polishing that emit plating-and-polishing metal HAP?
gates.test: yes -> one or more affected sources present (subject to subpart if area-source thresholds met); no -> those affected-source categories absent
gates.quote: This subpart applies to each new or existing affected source, as specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, at all times.

gates.question: Does the facility qualify as an area source under the numeric thresholds (i.e., not potential to emit a single HAP >=9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined HAP >=22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy))?
gates.test: yes -> facility is an area source (this subpart targets area sources); no -> facility may be a major source and subject to other NESHAPs
gates.quote: does not have the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams per year (Mg/yr) (10 tons per year (tpy)) or more

gates.question: Do any of the exclusions in §63.11505(d) apply (e.g., units subject to subpart N, research & development, educational, repair operations, polishing to restore original finish, or materials containing plating HAP below specified concentrations)?
gates.test: yes -> the listed excluded process/units are not subject to this subpart; no -> exclusions do not apply
gates.quote: Any plating or polishing process that uses process materials that contain cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel (as the metal) in amounts less than 0.1 percent by weight

Facility-level potential-to-emit estimates (to confirm area-source vs major-source status in practice)

Determine date of construction or reconstruction of each affected source (before or after April 3, 2008) to establish new vs existing status and applicable compliance deadlines.

candidates.title: Lime Manufacturing Plants (Subpart AAAAA)

gates.question: Does your plant qualify as a lime manufacturing plant (LMP) that manufactures lime product by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances?
gates.test: yes: proceed to affected_source gate; no: this subpart does not apply
gates.quote: An LMP is an establishment engaged in the manufacture of lime product (calcium oxide, calcium oxide with magnesium oxide, or dead burned dolomite) by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells or other calcareous substances.

gates.question: Is the emission unit in question a lime kiln (and if applicable its associated cooler or processed stone handling operations) located at an LMP?
gates.test: yes: proceed to major_or_area and threshold gates; no: this subpart does not apply to that unit
gates.quote: This subpart applies to each existing or new lime kiln(s) and their associated cooler(s), and processed stone handling (PSH) operations system(s) located at an LMP that is a major source.

gates.question: Is the LMP a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥9.07 megagrams (10 tons)/yr or any combination of HAP ≥22.68 megagrams (25 tons)/yr)?
gates.test: yes: subject to this subpart if other gates also met; no: plant may be area source (consider area-source rules or testing)
gates.quote: A major source of HAP is a plant site that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year from all emission sources at the plant site.

gates.question: Does the kiln produce lime product from stone feed by calcination (i.e., is it a lime kiln as defined: device used to produce lime product from stone feed by calcination)?
gates.test: yes: proceed (device meets lime kiln definition); no: this device may not be regulated as a lime kiln under this subpart
gates.quote: Lime kiln means the device, including any associated preheater, used to produce a lime product from stone feed by calcination.

gates.question: Is the LMP located at a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant, or does it only process sludge containing calcium carbonate from water softening processes?
gates.test: yes: subpart AAAAA excludes those LMPs; no: proceed with other applicability gates
gates.quote: unless the LMP is located at a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant, or only processes sludge containing calcium carbonate from water softening processes.

gates.question: Are you seeking to claim that the LMP is an area source of HAP (i.e., not a major source)?
gates.test: yes: you must measure HCl emissions from all lime kilns per required methods; no: proceed under major-source requirements
gates.quote: If you wish to claim that your LMP is an area source, you must measure the emissions of hydrogen chloride from all lime kilns, except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section, at your plant using either:

gates.question: Did construction or reconstruction of the affected source commence on or before January 5, 2023 (vs after July 16, 2024) for purposes of HCl/mercury/TOH/D/F compliance dates?
gates.test: yes: compliance date for those emissions limitations is July 16, 2027; no: different/new source compliance dates may apply
gates.quote: If your affected source commenced construction or reconstruction on or before January, 5, 2023, then the compliance date for HCl, mercury, total organic HAP, and D/F emissions limitations is July 16, 2027.

missing: Whether the kiln is calcining primary stone feed (limestone/dolomite/shells/other calcareous material) versus calcining recycled/internal lime mud from your process
Whether the plant is located at (or part of) a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, or beet sugar manufacturing plant (exemption list)
Confirmation of the plant's major-source status by emissions or potential-to-emit calculations (single and combined HAP rates)
Construction or reconstruction commencement date for the kiln (to determine new vs existing and applicable compliance dates)
Whether the kiln has associated coolers or processed stone handling operations that would be subject under §63.7082(a)

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

gates.question: Do the General Provisions in subpart A (40 CFR part 63, subpart A) apply to your source, or is applicability governed by subpart AAAAA where overlap exists?
gates.test: yes: follow subpart A as indicated in Table 9 unless subpart AAAAA takes precedence; no: subpart A may not apply or AAAAA takes precedence
gates.quote: Table 9 to this subpart shows which parts of the General Provisions in §§ 63.1 through 63.16 apply to you. When there is overlap between subpart A and subpart AAAAA, as indicated in the “Explanations” column in Table 8, subpart AAAAA takes precedence.

missing: Which specific parts of the General Provisions (§§63.1–63.16) apply to this LMP (Table 9) and the details in Table 8 showing any overlap or precedence

checklist.item: Confirm whether the kiln produces lime product from stone feed (limestone/dolomite/shells/other calcareous materials).
Confirm the plant's HAP major-source status with calculated or reported potential-to-emit (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined).
Confirm whether the facility is located at or part of any exempted industries (kraft/soda/sulfite pulp mill or beet sugar plant) or only processes water-softening CaCO3 sludge.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants from Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units

gates.question: Is the unit a coal-fired or oil-fired electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) as defined in this subpart?
gates.test: Yes => continue to affected_source gate. No => this subpart does not apply.
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 of this subpart.

gates.question: Is the unit part of the collection of coal- or oil-fired EGUs at the source (i.e., the affected source for this subpart)?
gates.test: Yes => continue to threshold gate. No => this subpart does not apply.
gates.quote: The affected source of this subpart is the collection of all existing coal- or oil-fired EGUs, as defined in § 63.10042, within a subcategory.

gates.question: Did the unit burn oil for more than 10.0 percent of average annual heat input (three previous calendar years) or more than 15.0 percent in any one of those years?
gates.test: Yes => the unit qualifies as an oil-fired EGU for this subpart (continue with compliance requirements). No => the unit does not meet the oil-fired EGU fuel threshold for this subpart.
gates.quote: and that burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years

missing: Whether the unit meets the "electric utility steam generating unit (EGU)" definition (net electrical output >25 MWe and serves a generator that produces electricity for sale).
Confirmation of three-year heat-input fuel shares (oil vs. natural gas) on the statutory basis (the three previous calendar years after the compliance date) in official records or permit projections.
Whether the unit is new, reconstructed, or existing relative to EGU rule dates (may affect certain provisions).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (Boiler MACT)

gates.question: Is the unit an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at or part of a major source of HAP?
gates.test: Yes => continue to affected_source/major_or_area gates. No => this subpart does not apply.
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater as defined in § 63.7575 that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP,

gates.question: Is the affected source the collection of boilers and process heaters at the major source that would include this unit?
gates.test: Yes => continue to exemption and major_or_area gates. No => this subpart does not apply.
gates.quote: The affected source of this subpart is the collection at a major source of all existing industrial, commercial, and institutional boilers and process heaters within a subcategory as defined in § 63.7575.

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP)?
gates.test: Yes => continue to exemption gate. No => this subpart does not apply (it's for major sources).
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater as defined in § 63.7575 that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP,

gates.question: Is the unit an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU, or a natural gas-fired EGU firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis (exclusion in § 63.7491)?
gates.test: Yes => the unit is excluded from subpart DDDDD. No => unit remains potentially subject to subpart DDDDD (if major source and other criteria met).
gates.quote: An electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU of this part or a natural gas-fired EGU as defined in subpart UUUUU of this part firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis.

gates.question: Was the boiler or process heater constructed after June 4, 2010 (i.e., is it new) for applicability/timing considerations?
gates.test: Yes => treat as new source under subpart DDDDD (different requirements/timing). No => treat as existing source (different requirements/timing).
gates.quote: A boiler or process heater is new if you commence construction of the boiler or process heater after June 4, 2010, and you meet the applicability criteria at the time you commence construction.

missing: Whether the unit is an EGU (net electrical output >25 MWe and produces electricity for sale) or is classified as an industrial/commercial/institutional boiler under § 63.7575.
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP (major source determination).
Annual heat input fraction from natural gas (to verify the ≥85% natural gas exclusion) and official three-year fuel usage records if needed.
Construction date of the unit (before or after June 4, 2010) to determine new vs existing status under this subpart.

checklist.item: Confirm the unit's net electrical output (MWe) and whether it serves a generator that produces electricity for sale (to determine if it meets the EGU definition).
Obtain verified three-year and single-year heat-input fuel shares (percent heat input from oil and from natural gas) to test the >10%/>15% oil thresholds and the ≥85% natural gas exclusion.
Determine whether the facility is classified as a major source of HAP (facility-wide major source status).
Verify whether the unit is listed as an electric utility steam generating unit covered by subpart UUUUU in permits or prior determinations (to test DDDDD exclusion).
Confirm unit construction or reconstruction date relative to June 4, 2010 (for Boiler MACT new/existing status).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Pesticide Active Ingredient (PAI) Production

gates.question: Is the process part of pesticide active ingredient manufacturing (PAI) that processes, uses, or produces pesticide active ingredients?
gates.test: yes: consider Subpart MMM; no: Subpart MMM not applicable
gates.quote: pesticide active ingredient manufacturing process units (PAI process units) that process, use, or produce HAP, and are located at a plant site that is a major source

gates.question: Will the new distillation column be part of (or assigned to) an existing PAI process unit (i.e., used to produce a PAI or integral intermediate) at the facility?
gates.test: yes: the equipment is part of an affected PAI process unit (consider MMM requirements); no: the equipment may not be subject to MMM
gates.quote: A PAI process unit consists of: the process, as defined in this subpart; associated storage vessels, as determined by the procedures in § 63.1360(f); equipment identified in § 63.1362(k);

gates.question: Is the plant site a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the CAA?
gates.test: yes: Subpart MMM may apply to the facility-wide PAI affected source; no: Subpart MMM does not apply
gates.quote: and are located at a plant site that is a major source, as defined in section 112(a) of the CAA.

gates.question: If the distillation is a dedicated PAI process unit (i.e., new dedicated equipment), does it have the potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any one HAP or ≥25 tpy of combined HAP?
gates.test: yes: the unit meets the definition of a new dedicated PAI process unit for MMM new-source provisions; no: it may be treated as an addition to an affected source but not a new dedicated PAI unit
gates.quote: Addition of new equipment to an affected source does not constitute construction, provided the new equipment is not a dedicated PAI process unit with the potential to emit 10 tons/yr of any one HAP or 25 tons/yr of combined HAP, but it may constitute reconstruction

gates.question: Is the distillation operation exempt from Subpart MMM (for example, research and development, PAI units subject to subpart F, coal tar distillation, vessels storing only impurities, or equipment intended to operate in organic HAP service <300 hours/yr)?
gates.test: yes: Subpart MMM does not apply to that equipment/operation; no: exemptions do not apply (consider full MMM applicability)
gates.quote: The provisions of this subpart do not apply to: (1) Research and development facilities; (2) PAI process units that are subject to subpart F of this part; (3) Production of ethylene; (4) Coal tar distillation;

gates.question: Is the distillation column being constructed or reconstructed after November 10, 1997 (i.e., would it be a 'new' affected source under MMM)?
gates.test: yes: new-source MMM requirements may apply; no: existing-source MMM requirements apply
gates.quote: A new affected source subject to this subpart and to which the requirements for new sources apply is defined according to the criteria in paragraph (b)(1) or (2) of this section. (1) An affected source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after November 10, 1997.

missing: Whether the distillation column will be used to produce the PAI (i.e., assigned to the PAI process unit) or is a separate/shared purification unit
Estimated potential-to-emit (tpy) of any individual HAP and combined HAP from the new distillation column
Construction/reconstruction start date for the distillation column
Whether the raw-material storage tanks in the neighboring building are assigned to the PAI process unit per §63.1360(f)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (MCPU)

gates.question: Is the process a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process unit (MCPU) located at (or part of) a major source of HAP?
gates.test: yes: consider Subpart FFFF for MCPU applicability; no: Subpart FFFF not applicable
gates.quote: You are subject to the requirements in this subpart if you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions

gates.question: Does the distillation column meet the definition of equipment 'included in an MCPU' (i.e., equipment necessary to operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process that satisfies the criteria in §63.2435(b)(1)-(3))?
gates.test: yes: the column is part of an MCPU and Subpart FFFF may apply; no: Subpart FFFF may not apply to that equipment
gates.quote: An MCPU includes equipment necessary to operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process, as defined in § 63.2550, that satisfies all of the conditions specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section.

gates.question: Is the affected source defined as the facilitywide collection of MCPU and associated systems (i.e., is the distillation within that facilitywide collection)?
gates.test: yes: facilitywide FFFF requirements may apply; no: FFFF may not apply facilitywide
gates.quote: The miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing affected source is the facilitywide collection of MCPU and heat exchange systems, wastewater, and waste management units that are associated with manufacturing materials described in § 63.2435(b)(1).

gates.question: If the distillation would be a dedicated MCPU, does it have the potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any one HAP or ≥25 tpy of combined HAP (i.e., subject to new-source MCPU criteria)?
gates.test: yes: new-source FFFF (dedicated MCPU) provisions may apply; no: may be existing-source or not a dedicated MCPU under FFFF
gates.quote: Each dedicated MCPU that has the potential to emit 10 tons per year (tpy) of any one HAP or 25 tpy of combined HAP, and you commenced construction or reconstruction of the MCPU after April 4, 2002.

gates.question: Is the operation exempt from Subpart FFFF (e.g., research and development, certain NAICS codes, affiliated operations covered by other subparts)?
gates.test: yes: Subpart FFFF does not apply to those exempt operations; no: exemptions do not apply
gates.quote: The requirements in this subpart do not apply to the operations specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (7) of this section. (1) Research and development facilities, as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA.

gates.question: Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source or MCPU commenced after April 4, 2002 (i.e., would it be treated as a new affected source under Subpart FFFF)?
gates.test: yes: new-source FFFF requirements may apply; no: existing-source FFFF requirements apply
gates.quote: Each affected source defined in paragraph (b) of this section for which you commenced construction or reconstruction after April 4, 2002, and you meet the applicability criteria at the time you commenced construction or reconstruction.

missing: Whether the material produced/handled by the distillation (the purified feedstock and any byproducts) falls within the SIC/NAICS/product descriptions in §63.2435(b)(1)
Whether the distillation column will be dedicated to one MCPU or serve multiple processes (dedicated vs. nondedicated)
Estimated potential-to-emit (tpy) of any individual and combined HAP from the distillation column
Whether the raw-material storage tanks in the neighboring building are assigned to the same MCPU per §63.2435(d)

candidates.title: General applicability for Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (subpart F; applicability to SOCMI/CMPU)

gates.question: Does the unit meet the criteria for a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) subject to subparts F, G, and H (i.e., manufacture listed chemicals, use listed organic HAP, and be at a major source)?
gates.test: yes: CMPU rules in subpart F (and related subparts) may apply; no: subpart F not applicable
gates.quote: the provisions of subparts F, G, and H of this part apply to chemical manufacturing process units that meet all the criteria specified in paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), and (b)(3) of this section:

gates.question: Is the distillation unit dedicated to (or assigned to) a chemical manufacturing process unit on-site according to the assignment rules for distillation units?
gates.test: yes: the distillation vents may be process vents for a CMPU and subject to subpart F/G/H; no: distillation may not be part of CMPU
gates.quote: Where a distillation unit is dedicated to a chemical manufacturing process unit, the distillation column shall be considered part of that chemical manufacturing process unit.

gates.question: Is the process located at a plant site that is a major source (section 112(a))?
gates.test: yes: CMPU provisions apply if other criteria met; no: CMPU provisions may not apply
gates.quote: chemical manufacturing process units that meet all the criteria specified in paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), and (b)(3) of this section: (3) Are located at a plant site that is a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Act.

gates.question: Does the addition of the distillation column constitute a new source (construction/reconstruction) because it has potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any one HAP or ≥25 tpy combined (thus triggering new-source CMPU requirements)?
gates.test: yes: new-source CMPU requirements apply; no: treat as existing-source addition (or not subject)
gates.quote: (iii) The addition has the potential to emit 10 tons per year or more of any HAP or 25 tons per year or more of any combination of HAP's, unless the Administrator establishes a lesser quantity.

gates.question: Is the distillation operation exempt from subparts F/G/H (e.g., research and development, petroleum refining process units, ethylene production units, batch process vents)?
gates.test: yes: the listed exemptions in §63.100(j) apply and subpart F does not cover that process; no: exemptions do not apply
gates.quote: The provisions of subparts F, G, and H of this part do not apply to the processes specified in paragraphs (j)(1) through (j)(6) of this section. (1) Research and development facilities, regardless of whether the facilities are located at the same plant site

gates.question: Would the distillation be a new source under subpart F (i.e., construction commenced after the dates set for new-source compliance) or an existing source (subject to existing-source compliance dates)?
gates.test: yes (new): comply with new-source dates in §63.100(k); no (existing): comply with existing-source dates in §63.100(k)
gates.quote: New sources that commence construction after August 26, 1996 shall be in compliance with this subpart F, subparts G and H of this part upon initial start-up or by January 17, 1997, whichever is later.

missing: Whether the distillation vent(s) meet the definition of a process vent for a CMPU (undiluted HAP concentrations, emission rates)
Whether the distillation unit is dedicated to a CMPU that manufactures a chemical listed in table 1 or uses listed organic HAP (per §63.100(b)(1)-(2))
Estimated potential-to-emit (tpy) of individual and combined HAP from the distillation column
Construction/reconstruction start date for the distillation column

checklist.item: Confirm whether the distillation column will be operated as part of the PAI production process (i.e., will the purified feedstock be directly fed to the herbicide PAI process) or as a separate/shared purification unit.
Identify whether the distillation column will be dedicated to a single process (dedicated PAI process unit or dedicated MCPU/CMPU) or shared among multiple processes.
Estimate potential-to-emit (tpy) for individual HAP and combined HAP from the new distillation column (including startup/shutdown emissions and storage/transfer connections).
Determine assignment of the neighboring building storage tanks (are they assigned to the PAI process unit/MCPU/CMPU per §63.1360(f)/§63.2435(d)/§63.100(g)?)

candidates.title: What definitions apply to this subpart?

gates.question: Is the operation a chemical preparation operation described by NAICS code 325998?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart may apply; no -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: Chemical preparation means a target HAP-containing product, or intermediate used in the manufacture of other products, manufactured in a process operation described by the NAICS code 325998

gates.question: Does the cathode slurry mixing equipment contain, contact, or process target HAP-containing materials (i.e., nickel compounds at or above the target HAP threshold)?
gates.test: yes -> equipment is in target HAP service and may be an affected source under this subpart; no -> this subpart likely does not apply to that equipment
gates.quote: In target HAP service means that equipment in the chemical preparation operation either contains, contacts, or is processing target HAP-containing materials.

gates.question: Is the equipment used primarily for research and development rather than manufacture for commercial sale?
gates.test: yes -> the research and development exemption may apply and the subpart may not apply; no -> exemption does not apply
gates.quote: Research and development equipment means any equipment whose primary purpose is to conduct research and development to develop new processes and products

missing: Whether the facility operation is classified under NAICS code 325998
Measured or supplier-reported nickel concentration in the active material and slurry (percent by weight)
Whether the facility is an area source or a major source of HAPs
Whether the mixing equipment is used exclusively for R&D or for commercial production

candidates.title: What are the standards for new and existing paints and allied products manufacturing facilities?

gates.question: Does the facility perform paints and allied products manufacturing and is it an area source that processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP?
gates.test: yes -> this paints and allied products subpart may apply; no -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions and processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP,

gates.question: Do the paints and allied products manufacturing processes at the facility include the slurry mixing and coating operations that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP?
gates.test: yes -> those processes are the affected source under this subpart; no -> they are not the affected source under this subpart
gates.quote: The affected source consists of all paints and allied products manufacturing processes that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP at the facility.

gates.question: Is the facility a research and development facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7)?
gates.test: yes -> the standards of this subpart do not apply; no -> the exemption does not apply
gates.quote: The standards of this subpart do not apply to research and development facilities, as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA.

missing: Whether the cathode slurry and process are classified as 'paints and allied products manufacturing' under the subpart definitions/NAICS
Whether the facility qualifies as an area source of HAPs
Whether the slurry/coating materials are considered 'materials containing HAP' under this subpart (nickel content, other HAPs)

candidates.title: What are the applicability requirements and compliance dates?

gates.question: Is there a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) at the facility (NAICS 325) that meets the CMPU applicability conditions?
gates.test: yes -> this CMPU subpart may apply to those units; no -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, you are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that meets the conditions specified in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section.

gates.question: Does the CMPU include the process vessels, equipment, and activities (mixing vessels, storage, transfers) used to operate the chemical manufacturing process for the material?
gates.test: yes -> those items are included in the affected source for the CMPU; no -> they are not part of the affected source for the CMPU
gates.quote: A CMPU includes all process vessels, equipment, and activities necessary to operate a chemical manufacturing process that produces a material or a family of materials described by North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 325.

gates.question: Does the CMPU use as feedstock any material that contains manganese or trivalent chromium >1.0% by weight, or any other Table 1 HAP (including metal HAP) at >0.1% by weight?
gates.test: yes -> CMPU is subject to this subpart for Table 1 HAP control; no -> CMPU may not be subject based on Table 1 HAP thresholds
gates.quote: The CMPU uses as feedstock, any material that contains quinoline, manganese, and/or trivalent chromium at an individual concentration greater than 1.0 percent by weight, or any other Table 1 HAP at an individual concentration greater than 0.1 percent by weight.

missing: Whether the cathode slurry manufacturing falls under NAICS 325 (chemical manufacturing) or another NAICS (e.g., battery manufacturing)
Measured or supplier-reported concentrations of nickel or other Table 1 HAP in feedstocks or liquid streams
Whether the operation is excluded by paragraph (c) (e.g., if it is covered by the paints and allied products subpart)
Whether the facility is an area source (vs major)

candidates.title: What parts of my plant does this subpart cover?

gates.question: Does the facility perform surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products in one of the listed subcategories?
gates.test: yes -> this surface coating subpart may apply; no -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: The affected source is the collection of all of the items listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section that are used for surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products within each subcategory.

gates.question: Are the mixing vessels and storage containers used to store or mix the cathode slurry considered 'storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners and/or other additives, and cleaning materials are stored or mixed'?
gates.test: yes -> those vessels are part of the affected source for surface coating; no -> they are not part of the affected source under this subpart
gates.quote: All coating operations as defined in § 63.3981; (2) All storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners and/or other additives, and cleaning materials are stored or mixed;

missing: Whether the cathode slurry is a 'coating' covered by the subpart definitions and applied to miscellaneous metal parts or products (e.g., foil as a product)
Whether the facility/line falls within the subcategories listed at § 63.3881(a) (not provided)
Whether the operation is area source status and whether HAP-containing coatings are used

checklist.item: Confirm whether the mixing vessels contain or process nickel-containing materials at or above the target HAP threshold (e.g., ≥0.1% nickel by weight).
Confirm the facility NAICS code for the cathode slurry operation (is it NAICS 325998 or another NAICS?).
Confirm whether the cathode slurry is characterized as a 'paint/coating/allied product' or as a chemical preparation (supplier formulation, SDS, product description).
Confirm whether the equipment is used for research and development only or for commercial production.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Glass Manufacturing Area Source

gates.question: Does the plant operate a glass manufacturing facility that melts raw materials to produce molten glass and form it into sheets, containers, or other shapes?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: A glass manufacturing facility is a plant site that manufactures flat glass, glass containers, or pressed and blown glass by melting a mixture of raw materials, as defined in § 63.11459, to produce molten glass

gates.question: Does the facility have an affected glass melting furnace located at a glass manufacturing facility that satisfies the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3)?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: This subpart applies to each existing or new affected glass melting furnace that is located at a glass manufacturing facility and satisfies the requirements specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section.

gates.question: Is the source an area source of HAP emissions (i.e., below the single-HAP and total-HAP numeric thresholds)?
gates.test: yes -> candidate is an area-source rule candidate; no -> major-source thresholds apply and this area-source rule may not be applicable
gates.quote: An area source of HAP emissions is any stationary source or group of stationary sources within a contiguous area under common control that does not have the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams per year (Mg/yr) (10 tons per year (tpy)) or more

gates.question: Does the furnace produce glass that contains glass manufacturing metal HAP at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy)?
gates.test: yes -> furnace meets the production-rate threshold in the subpart; no -> furnace does not meet this subpart's rate threshold
gates.quote: The furnace is used to produce glass, which contains one or more of the glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials, at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy).

missing: Whether frit production (melting and quenching into frit) is considered 'producing molten glass and forming the molten glass into ... other shapes' under the subpart's definition (i.e., whether frit counts as 'other shapes').
Whether the furnace used for frit production is a continuous furnace as defined in § 63.11459.
Annual production rate of the furnace (Mg/yr or tpy) for comparison to the 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) threshold.
Confirmation that glass manufacturing metal HAP are charged as raw materials in the batch formulation (the text requires compounds of glass manufacturing metal HAP).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Paints and Allied Products Area Source

gates.question: Does the facility perform paints and allied products manufacturing as an area source and process, use, or generate materials containing HAP?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions and processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP, as defined in § 63.11607.

gates.question: Does the affected source consist of all paints and allied products manufacturing processes at the facility that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: The affected source consists of all paints and allied products manufacturing processes that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP at the facility.

gates.question: Are the products manufactured intended to be applied to a substrate and to leave a dried film of solid material (i.e., are they 'paints and allied products')?
gates.test: yes -> operations are within the paints-and-allied-products definition; no -> paints subpart likely not applicable
gates.quote: Paints and allied products means materials such as paints, inks, adhesives, stains, varnishes, shellacs, putties, sealers, caulks, and other coatings from raw materials that are intended to be applied to a substrate

missing: Whether frit is produced as a material intended to be applied to a substrate and to leave a dried film (i.e., whether frit functions as a 'paint' or 'coating' under the definition).
Whether the manufacturing operations for frit are the typical paints-and-allied-products operations (blending/mixing) versus melting and quenching.
Confirmation of NAICS classification applicability (though NAICS 3255 is referenced in the paints definition, need to confirm the specific product/process falls within the paints subpart scope).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Chemical Preparations Area Source

gates.question: Is the operation a 'chemical preparation' manufactured in a process operation described by NAICS code 325998 (i.e., is the facility a chemical preparations facility under § 63.11588)?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: Chemical preparation means a target HAP-containing product, or intermediate used in the manufacture of other products, manufactured in a process operation described by the NAICS code 325998 if the operation manufactures target HAP-containing products

gates.question: Does the facility meet all of the conditions: (1) own/operate a chemical preparations facility, (2) the facility is a stationary area source of HAP, and (3) it has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you meet all of the following conditions: (1) You own or operate a chemical preparations facility (as defined in § 63.11588, "What definitions apply to this subpart?"), (2) The chemical preparations facility is a stationary area source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) (as defined in § 63.2), and (3) The chemical preparations facility has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service (as defined in § 63.11588, "What definitions apply to this subpart?")

missing: Whether the frit production operation is described by NAICS 325998 (chemical preparations) rather than NAICS 3255, and whether the specific operations (mixing, blending, milling, extruding) match the 'chemical preparations operation' definition.
Whether the operation is in 'target HAP service' (target HAP includes nickel compounds per § 63.11588, but need confirmation of concentrations meeting target HAP thresholds).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (CMPU rule)

gates.question: Does the facility own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that meets the CMPU subpart conditions?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, you are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that meets the conditions specified in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section.

gates.question: Is the CMPU located at an area source and are Table 1 HAP present in the CMPU as specified in paragraph (a)(2)?
gates.test: yes -> candidate continues; no -> candidate not applicable
gates.quote: The CMPU is located at an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions. HAP listed in table 1 to this subpart (Table 1 HAP) are present in the CMPU, as specified in paragraph (a)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), or (iv) of this section.

gates.question: Does the CMPU use feedstock containing quinoline, manganese, and/or trivalent chromium at >1.0% by weight, or any other Table 1 HAP at >0.1% by weight (per paragraph (a)(2)(i))?
gates.test: yes -> Table 1 HAP criterion met; no -> CMPU may not meet Table 1 HAP presence criterion
gates.quote: The CMPU uses as feedstock, any material that contains quinoline, manganese, and/or trivalent chromium at an individual concentration greater than 1.0 percent by weight, or any other Table 1 HAP at an individual concentration greater than 0.1 percent by weight.

gates.question: Is the CMPU operation excluded because it is part of a chemical manufacturing area source category listed in paragraph (c)(1), such as Manufacture of Paint and Allied Products subject to subpart CCCCCCC?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart does not apply (excluded); no -> continue evaluation under this subpart
gates.quote: This subpart does not apply to the operations specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (6) of this section. (1) Affected sources under the following chemical manufacturing area source categories listed pursuant to Clean Air Act (CAA) section 112(c)(3) and 112(k)(3)(B)(ii)

missing: Whether frit production is a CMPU as defined (NAICS 325 product) and whether the CMPU uses any Table 1 HAP (manganese, chromium, quinoline, or others listed in Table 1) at concentrations above the thresholds in paragraph (a)(2).
Whether the operation falls within the exclusions in paragraph (c) (e.g., manufacture of paints and allied products subject to subpart CCCCCCC).

Identification of the Table 1 HAP list and whether nickel (specifically present in your raw materials) appears on Table 1 for purposes of this subpart (provided text references 'Table 1' but table content not given).

checklist.item: Confirm whether frit production involves melting raw materials to produce molten glass and forming the molten glass into shapes (i.e., whether frit counts as 'producing molten glass and forming ... other shapes').
Determine whether the furnace used for frit production is a continuous furnace (per definitions referenced by the glass subpart).
Provide the annual production rate for the furnace (Mg/yr or tpy) to compare to the 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) threshold in the glass subpart.
Confirm whether the frit product is intended to be applied to a substrate and leave a dried film (i.e., meets 'paints and allied products' definition).
Confirm the facility NAICS code for the frit operation (is it NAICS 325998 chemical preparations or NAICS 3255 paints/other).

Provide analytical or formulation data (e.g., SDS) showing concentrations of Table 1 HAP (manganese, chromium, quinoline, others) or target HAP (nickel) in feedstocks to test CMPU and chemical-preparations criteria.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units

gates.question: Is the unit a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042?
gates.test: Yes -> continue applicability evaluation under this subpart; No -> this subpart does not apply to the unit
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 of this subpart.

gates.question: Does the unit serve a generator that produces electricity for sale (i.e., meet the EGU definition such as >25 MWe or qualifying cogeneration)?
gates.test: Yes -> unit meets the EGU definition element; No -> unit may not be an EGU under this subpart
gates.quote: Electric utility steam generating unit means a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit of more than 25 megawatts electric (MWe) that serves a generator that produces electricity for sale.

gates.question: Is the unit a stationary combustion turbine designated as a major-source or area-source stationary combustion turbine subject to subpart YYYY?
gates.test: Yes -> unit is excluded from this subpart under §63.9983(a); No -> proceed with this subpart applicability
gates.quote: Any unit designated as a major source stationary combustion turbine subject to subpart YYYY of this part and any unit designated as an area source stationary combustion turbine, other than an integrated gasification combined cycle (IGCC) unit.

gates.question: Does the unit burn oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years (or more than 15.0 percent in any one year) such that it is an oil-fired EGU?
gates.test: Yes -> unit meets the oil-fired EGU fuel-threshold to be subject to this subpart; No -> may be a natural-gas or other excluded EGU
gates.quote: and that burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years after the compliance date for your facility

gates.question: Does the unit qualify as a limited-use liquid oil-fired EGU (per the limited-use definition) such that it is not subject to Tables 1 and 2 emission limits but must follow tune-up work practices in Table 3?
gates.test: Yes -> emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 do not apply and tune-up work practice requirements apply; No -> emission limits apply except during startup/shutdown per rule
gates.quote: then you are not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2, but you must comply with the performance tune-up work practice requirements in Table 3.

gates.question: During the auxiliary-steam-only firing, does the operation meet the definition of 'startup' (i.e., does startup end when any steam is used to generate electricity for sale or for any other purpose including on-site use)?
gates.test: Yes -> that period is defined as startup (work practices apply during startup/ shutdown for oil-fired EGUs); No -> operation is not startup and emission limits apply
gates.quote: Startup ends when any of the steam from the boiler is used to generate electricity for sale or for any other purpose (including on-site use).

gates.question: Are you relying on the alternative startup definition (startup begins with firing for any purpose, including useful thermal energy) that was allowed prior to January 2, 2025?
gates.test: Yes -> the alternative (broader) startup definition may be used only for incidents prior to the statutory cutoff; No -> only the primary startup definition applies
gates.quote: Startup begins with either the firing of any fuel in an EGU for the purpose of producing electricity or useful thermal energy (such as heat or steam) for industrial, commercial, heating, or cooling purposes

gates.question: If the period is considered startup, must work practice requirements from Table 3 be applied instead of the numeric emission limits during that period?
gates.test: Yes -> apply Table 3 startup/shutdown work practices for coal- or oil-fired EGUs; No -> apply emission limits at all times
gates.quote: you are required to meet the work practice requirements, items 3 and 4, in Table 3 to this subpart during periods of startup or shutdown.

missing: Whether the specific boiler(s) are >25 MWe and serve a generator that produces electricity for sale (or meet cogeneration criteria)
Three-year fuel use history (percent of heat input from residual oil vs. other fuels) to confirm oil-fired EGU threshold (>10% average or >15% any year)
Whether the auxiliary-steam-only operation uses the steam for any other purpose (including on-site use) or leads to electricity generation or sale
Whether the unit is claimed as a limited-use liquid oil-fired EGU (capacity factor when burning oil <8% averaged over 24-month block)
Whether the owner/operator intends to rely on the pre-January 2, 2025 alternative startup definition for any incidents and the dates of those incidents
Whether the unit is actually a stationary combustion turbine (to consider exclusion under subpart YYYY)

gates.quote: Any unit designated as a major source stationary combustion turbine subject to subpart YYYY of this part and any unit designated as an area source stationary combustion turbine, other than an integrated gasification combined cycle (IGCC) unit.

gates.test: Yes -> the unit may be an industrial boiler subject to Subpart DDDDD rather than UUUUU; No -> Subpart DDDDD exclusion does not apply

gates.test: yes: Unit 1 meets the EGU source category and proceed to equipment-level tests; no: Unit 1 is not an EGU subject to this subpart.
gates.quote: Electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) means a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit of more than 25 megawatts electric (MWe) that serves a generator that produces electricity for sale.

gates.question: Does Unit 1 qualify as an oil-fired electric utility steam generating unit (i.e., it burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years or more than 15.0 percent in any one of those years)?

gates.quote: Except as specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, you must be in compliance with the emission limits and work practice standards in Tables 1 through 5 to this subpart at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.

missing: Whether the filter step is performed as a separation/purification step that isolates a component (versus routine finishing of a formulated coating product)
Whether any separated component is transferred to another vessel for subsequent formulation and whether it is stored prior to formulation
HAP composition and concentrations of feedstocks/products and whether the facility is a major source of HAP
Whether the filtering occurs inside a process vessel as defined by the coatings rule or is part of ancillary/affiliated operations (e.g., cleaning, tinting)

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (MCPU)

gates.question: Does your unit operate as a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process (MCPU) producing organic chemicals or materials described by this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> the operation may be in the MCPU source category; no -> this subpart's source-category gate fails (consider other subparts).
gates.quote: miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions

gates.question: Does the equipment collectively function to operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process (including reaction, recovery, separation, purification, or other steps to produce a product or isolated intermediate)?
gates.test: yes -> the equipment may be part of an MCPU and subject to subpart FFFF; no -> this subpart's affected-source gate fails (operation may not be an MCPU).
gates.quote: An MCPU includes equipment necessary to operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process, as defined in § 63.2550, that satisfies all of the conditions specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section.

gates.question: Is the MCPU located at or part of a major source of HAP emissions?
gates.test: yes -> MCPU applicability to subpart FFFF is satisfied; no -> if area source, subpart FFFF may not apply (consider area-source rules).
gates.quote: miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions

gates.question: Does the process include separation, recovery, or purification steps (e.g., filtration) used to produce a product or isolated intermediate?
gates.test: yes -> these unit operations are within the definition of an MCPU process (supports subpart FFFF applicability); no -> absence of separation steps weighs against MCPU classification.
gates.quote: For the purposes of this subpart, process includes any, all or a combination of reaction, recovery, separation, purification, or other activity, operation, manufacture, or treatment which are used to produce a product or isolated intermediate.

gates.question: Are these operations ‘affiliated operations’ located at an affected source under specified coating subparts (mixing/dissolving of coating ingredients, coating mixing for viscosity adjustment, cleaning of coating lines, handling/storage of coatings and solvent, conveyance/treatment of wastewater)?
gates.test: yes -> such affiliated operations may be excluded from subpart FFFF and remain subject to the coating subpart; no -> no affiliated-operation exemption (subpart FFFF may apply).
gates.quote: Affiliated operations include, but are not limited to, mixing or dissolving of coating ingredients; coating mixing for viscosity adjustment, color tint or additive blending, or pH adjustment; cleaning of coating lines and coating line parts; handling and storage of coatings and solvent; and conveyance and treatment of wastewater;

missing: Whether the epoxy dispersion and final filtration are part of an organic chemical manufacturing process that produces an organic chemical or isolated intermediate (per MCPU definitions)
Whether the filtered material is an intermediate or the final coating product and how it is transferred/stored after filtration
NAICS classification of the process (whether it falls within MCPU NAICS exceptions in §63.2435(c)(5))
Quantities and HAP contents (to confirm major-source status and whether thresholds for Groups apply)

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

gates.question: Is the operation surface coating of plastic parts/products (coating application to a substrate with associated activities directly related to application)?
gates.test: yes -> operation may fall in plastic-parts surface-coating source category; no -> this subpart's source-category gate fails (operation not surface coating).
gates.quote: the source category to which this subpart applies is the surface coating of any plastic parts or products, as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.

gates.question: Does the facility use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP for surface coating of plastic parts/products and is the facility a major source or part of a major source of HAP?
gates.test: yes -> the source meets this subpart's affected-source applicability threshold; no -> this subpart may not apply (below thresholds or not a major source).
gates.quote: uses 378 liters (100 gallons (gal)) per year, or more, of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in the surface coating of plastic parts and products

gates.question: Does the facility emit or have the potential to emit a single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg (10 tons) per year or combined HAP ≥ 22.68 Mg (25 tons) per year (i.e., is it a major source)?
gates.test: yes -> the facility is a major source (subpart PPPP applies if coating thresholds met); no -> area-source status may preclude this subpart's applicability.
gates.quote: that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (Mg) (10 tons) or more per year

gates.question: Does the facility use only coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (per exemption)?
gates.test: yes -> the facility is excluded from this subpart under the no-organic-HAP exemption; no -> the exemption does not apply and subpart PPPP may apply if other criteria met.
gates.quote: A coating operation conducted at a facility where the facility uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, as determined according to § 63.3941(a).

gates.question: Are the activities not directly related to coating application (e.g., upstream manufacturing steps) such that they do not comprise ‘surface coating’ under this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> those activities are not part of this surface-coating subpart and may instead fall under manufacturing subparts; no -> activities are directly related to application and remain in this subpart's scope.
gates.quote: However, these activities do not comprise surface coating if they are not directly related to the application of the coating.

missing: Whether the described epoxy dispersion process includes surface-application steps (spray/dip) or is strictly upstream manufacturing of a coating product
Whether the facility uses ≥100 gallons/year of HAP-containing coatings in surface-coating operations (to meet PPPP threshold)
Whether the filtering is part of coating application-associated activities (mixing/cleaning) or a separate manufacturing/separation step upstream

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Process / CMPU definitions (Subpart VVVVVV)

gates.question: Does the operation constitute a chemical manufacturing process (CMPU) that collectively functions to produce a product or isolated intermediate?
gates.test: yes -> the operation may be considered a CMPU under chemical-manufacturing NESHAPs; no -> CMPU rules may not apply.
gates.quote: Chemical manufacturing process means all equipment which collectively functions to produce a product or isolated intermediate. A process includes, but is not limited to any, all, or a combination of reaction, recovery, separation, purification.

gates.question: Is the filtration/finishing step performed in a process vessel (e.g., centrifuge, mixing vessel, process tank) used in processing raw materials to chemical products?
gates.test: yes -> the equipment is a process vessel and may be subject to CMPU process-vent/vent-stream rules; no -> if not a process vessel, CMPU vessel-specific requirements may not apply.
gates.quote: Process vessel means each vessel, except hand-held containers, used in the processing of raw materials to chemical products. Examples include, but are not limited to centrifuges, mixing vessels, and process tanks.

missing: Whether the filtration unit is a process vessel as defined by CMPU rules or an ancillary/packaging/finished-product handling vessel
Whether the operation produces a product or isolated intermediate (i.e., is a CMPU) or is solely a formulation/finishing step tied to surface-coating application
HAP content of streams and whether process vents or wastewater thresholds are met (to determine process-vent or wastewater controls)

checklist.item: Confirm whether the filtration step is a separation/recovery/purification activity that isolates a formulation component (i.e., is it a 'separation activity' or 'recovery' step?).
Confirm whether any separated component is transferred to another vessel for subsequent formulation and whether it is stored prior to formulation (key to coatings exclusion).
Confirm whether the operation manufactures coatings (materials produced by blending/mixing/diluting/formulating) versus performing surface-coating application to substrates.
Confirm facility major-source status (single HAP ≥10 tpy or combined HAP ≥25 tpy) and HAP quantities in feedstocks/products.
Confirm NAICS/classification and whether the equipment is affiliated with another affected source/subpart (e.g., coating NESHAPs) or shared with an MCPU.
