candidates.title: Petroleum Refining (Subpart CC)

gates.question: Is the facility a petroleum refinery plant site that is a major source under section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act?
gates.test: yes: proceed to affected-source questions; no: this subpart (CC) does not apply.
gates.quote: Are located at a plant site that is a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act;

gates.question: Is the truck loading rack an emission point that falls within the affected source (e.g., a gasoline loading rack or a miscellaneous process vent) listed for this subpart?
gates.test: yes: evaluate equipment/control-device type under this subpart; no: this particular subpart CC affected-source listing may not include the rack.
gates.quote: Gasoline loading rack means the loading arms, pumps, meters, shutoff valves, relief valves, and other piping and valves necessary to fill gasoline cargo tanks.

gates.question: Is the combustor an enclosed combustion device (e.g., incinerator, boiler, or process heater) rather than a flare (a combustion device lacking an enclosed combustion chamber)?
gates.test: yes: device is an enclosed combustion device and is not a flare; no: device may qualify as a flare and flare requirements should be considered.
gates.quote: Flare means a combustion device lacking an enclosed combustion chamber that uses an uncontrolled volume of ambient air to burn gases.

gates.question: Is the emission point (loading rack/vent) located at the plant site that meets the major-source criterion for this subpart?
gates.test: yes: continue evaluation under subpart CC; no: this subpart CC does not apply.
gates.quote: Are located at a plant site that is a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act;

gates.question: Does the combustor meet the definition of a combustion device in this subpart (i.e., an individual unit such as a flare, incinerator, process heater, or boiler used for combustion of organic HAP vapors)?
gates.test: yes: device is a combustion device as defined and subject to the subpart's control/monitoring distinctions; no: the device may not be covered as a combustion device under this subpart.
gates.quote: Combustion device means an individual unit of equipment such as a flare, incinerator, process heater, or boiler used for the combustion of organic hazardous air pollutant vapors.

gates.question: If the control device is a flare, is the operation/date on or after January 30, 2019 so that §63.670 flare requirements apply?
gates.test: yes: if device is a flare, §63.670 applies; no: prior to that date alternative provisions (e.g., §63.11(b) or earlier rules) might apply.
gates.quote: Reduce emissions of organic HAP's using a flare. On and after January 30, 2019, the flare shall meet the requirements of § 63.670.

missing: Whether the Plant 2 loading rack is a gasoline loading rack (SIC 2911) or another type of miscellaneous process vent.
Whether the loading rack qualifies as Group 1 (e.g., gasoline throughput / Group 1 criteria) under the gasoline definitions.
Whether the vapor discharge from the truck loading rack is routed to the combustor as a control device (i.e., is the combustor the intended control for that vent stream?).
Whether the combustor has an enclosed combustion chamber (design details) or instead is an open/vented device that allows uncontrolled ambient air entrainment (i.e., meets the "flare" definition).
Whether the plant site meets the major source definition in practice (actual emissions and CAA 112(a) status).

candidates.title: Gasoline Loading Racks (Subpart R) — referenced by CC

gates.question: Is the truck loading rack a gasoline loading rack classified under SIC code 2911 and meeting the Group 1 criteria (bulk terminal throughput threshold)?
gates.test: yes: subpart R provisions may apply (and CC §63.650 ties loading racks to subpart R); no: subpart R likely does not apply.
gates.quote: Group 1 gasoline loading rack means any gasoline loading rack classified under Standard Industrial Classification code 2911 that is located within a bulk gasoline terminal that has a gasoline throughput greater than 75,700 liters per day.

gates.question: If a flare is used as the control device for the loading rack, is the flare subject to §63.670 on or after January 30, 2019 (per the gasoline loading rack provisions)?
gates.test: yes: flare must meet §63.670; no: prior rules or different subpart R requirements might have applied earlier.
gates.quote: If a flare is used as a control device, on and after January 30, 2019, the flare shall meet the requirements of § 63.670.

missing: Whether the specific truck loading rack in Plant 2 is a gasoline loading rack (SIC 2911) and whether it meets Group 1 throughput criteria.
Whether the combustor is the control device for that loading rack vent stream (i.e., the rack's vapors are routed to that combustor).
Physical/design details of the combustor (enclosed chamber vs open flare tip) for classification.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) — referenced by CC

gates.question: If relying on pre-2019 provisions, was the flare (or vent control) meeting §63.11(b) of subpart A prior to January 30, 2019?
gates.test: yes: prior-to-2019 subpart A provisions (§63.11(b)) might have been the applicable flare standard; no: §63.670 (CC) is the governing standard on/after Jan 30, 2019.
gates.quote: Reduce emissions of organic HAP's using a flare. On and after January 30, 2019, the flare shall meet the requirements of § 63.670.

missing: Whether any pre-2019 compliance demonstration under §63.11(b) or other Subpart A provisions exists for the combustor/flare in question.
Text or determinations under §63.11(b) as applied to this specific combustor (not included in the provided sections).

checklist.item: Confirm whether the Plant 2 truck loading rack is a gasoline loading rack (SIC 2911) and if so determine its gasoline throughput to establish Group 1/Group 2 status.
Confirm whether vapors from the truck loading rack are routed to the enclosed combustor as the control device.
Obtain design/specifications of the combustor: does it have an enclosed combustion chamber (incinerator/boiler/process heater) or is it an open flare tip (lacking enclosed chamber)?
Confirm the plant site's major-source status under CAA section 112(a).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Paper and Other Web Coating

gates.question: Does your facility operate web coating lines (web substrates with coating operations)?
gates.test: yes -> your facility operates the source category covered by this subpart; no -> this subpart's web-coating provisions do not apply
gates.quote: The provisions of this subpart apply to each new and existing facility that is a major source of HAP, as defined in § 63.2, at which web coating lines are operated.

gates.question: Is the mica line a continuous web coating line (coating applied across a continuous web between an unwind/feed and a rewind/cutting station)?
gates.test: yes -> that line meets the definition of an affected source (web coating line) for this subpart; no -> that line is not a web coating line under this subpart
gates.quote: Web coating line means any number of work stations, of which one or more applies a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating material across the entire width or any portion of the width of a web substrate

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of HAP as defined in § 63.2 (i.e., meets the major source threshold)?
gates.test: yes -> the facility meets the major-source criterion in this subpart and the subpart can apply; no -> this subpart applies only to major sources and would not apply
gates.quote: The provisions of this subpart apply to each new and existing facility that is a major source of HAP, as defined in § 63.2, at which web coating lines are operated.

gates.question: Are all coatings applied at your web coating lines non-HAP below the thresholds specified for non-HAP coatings?
gates.test: yes -> you may qualify for the non-HAP reporting exemption described in this subpart; no -> normal HAP requirements and demonstrations apply
gates.quote: have organic HAP contents below 0.1 percent by mass for OSHA-defined carcinogens as specified in section A.6.4 of appendix A to 29 CFR 1910.1200, and below 1.0 percent by mass for other organic HAP compounds

gates.question: Do all subject web coating lines at the facility utilize only non-HAP coatings so you can request the reporting exemption?
gates.test: yes -> you can become exempt from the reporting requirements (after submitting the required one-time report); no -> reporting and compliance demonstrations are required
gates.quote: If all of the subject web coating lines at your facility utilize non-HAP coatings, you can become exempt from the reporting requirements of this subpart

gates.question: Was the web coating line constructed or reconstructed after September 13, 2000 (i.e., is it a new affected source)?
gates.test: yes -> treat the line as a new affected source (different numeric limits may apply); no -> treat the line as an existing affected source
gates.quote: Existing affected source means any affected source the construction or reconstruction of which is commenced on or before September 13, 2000, and has not undergone reconstruction as defined in § 63.2.

missing: Whether the mica roll-to-roll line is operated as a continuous flexible web (wound/unwound) with coating applied between an unwind/feed and a rewind/cutting station
Whether the sheet-handled line is operated as individual sheets (not a continuous web)
Formulation data for the coatings used (organic HAP content or VOC/solids data) on each line
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP (total and single-HAP potential-to-emit in tpy)
Date of construction or reconstruction of each web coating line to determine new vs existing source status
Whether any control devices (capture systems, oxidizers, solvent recovery) are installed and how work stations are classified (always-, intermittently-, never-controlled)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Refractory Products Manufacturing

gates.question: Does your plant site manufacture refractory products (e.g., refractory bricks, shapes, monolithics, kiln furniture, crucibles, or other high-temperature lining materials)?
gates.test: yes -> the facility matches the refractory products manufacturing source category which this subpart addresses; no -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: A refractory products manufacturing facility is a plant site that manufactures refractory products (refractory bricks, refractory shapes, monolithics, kiln furniture, crucibles, and other materials used for lining furnaces and other high temperature process units), as defined in § 63.9824.

gates.question: Do the finished mica insulation products meet the regulatory definition of a 'refractory product' (nonmetallic, containing less than 50 percent carbon by weight, and having chemical/physical properties making them applicable for structures or components of systems)?
gates.test: yes -> the finished mica insulation would fall within the refractory product definition; no -> the finished mica insulation would not meet the refractory product definition in this subpart
gates.quote: Refractory product means nonmetallic materials containing less than 50 percent carbon by weight and having those chemical and physical properties that make them applicable for structures, or as components of systems

gates.question: Is the refractory products manufacturing facility located at or part of a major source of HAP (e.g., emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP)?

gates.quote: Area source means any stationary source of hazardous air pollutants that is not a major source as defined in this part.

gates.question: Are Table 1 HAP present in the CMPU at the concentration thresholds listed in §63.11494(a)(2) (e.g., >0.1% for most Table 1 organics, >1.0% for quinoline etc.)?
gates.test: yes -> the CMPU meets the Table 1 HAP presence threshold and is within the subpart's scope; no -> this subpart's CMPU-specific requirements do not apply.
gates.quote: HAP listed in table 1 to this subpart (Table 1 HAP) are present in the CMPU, as specified in paragraph (a)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), or (iv) of this section.

gates.question: Has a federally-enforceable control device been installed on an affected CMPU and is that control device necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area source levels?
gates.test: yes -> if the control device is federally enforceable and necessary to keep your emissions at area-source levels, this subpart requires obtaining a Title V (part 70/71) permit; no -> this subpart does not require Title V permitting on that basis (you may still need a permit for other reasons).
gates.quote: Any area source that installed a federally-enforceable control device on an affected CMPU is required to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71

gates.question: If you become subject to Title V under this subpart because of a control device, did you become subject by December 21, 2012 (or after)?
gates.test: yes -> complete Title V application required by December 21, 2013; no -> if you become subject after Dec 21, 2012, a complete application is due within 12 months after becoming subject.
gates.quote: For new and existing sources subject to this rule on December 21, 2012 and subject to title V as a result of this rule, a complete title V permit application must be submitted no later than December 21, 2013.

missing: Whether the CMPU actually contains Table 1 HAP at or above the concentrations specified in §63.11494(a)(2) (feedstock, byproduct, product, or generated concentrations).
Whether the control device is included in a federally enforceable limitation (e.g., in a permit or other enforceable mechanism).

Whether the control device is necessary to maintain the facility's emissions at area-source levels (i.e., without the control device the emissions or potential to emit would rise to major-source levels).
Whether the control device applies to the affected CMPU(s) that trigger subpart VVVVVV coverage (control must be on the affected CMPU).
Dates: when the control device/limits became federally enforceable (to determine applicable Title V application deadlines).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Part 63)

gates.question: Does the relevant area-source standard (or this part) explicitly give States the option to exclude area sources subject to that standard from the requirement to obtain a Title V permit?
gates.test: yes -> if the standard grants the State an exclusion option, check whether your State has exercised that option; no -> if the standard fails to specify, area sources affected by the standard are subject to Title V by default.
gates.quote: (i) States will have the option to exclude area sources affected by that standard from the requirement to obtain a title V permit

missing: Whether the State permitting authority for Ohio has exercised any option to exclude area sources under §63.1(c)(2)(i) for this specific standard or otherwise (i.e., whether Ohio's part 70 program excludes these area sources).
Whether the relevant standard (VVVVVV) or implementing rulemaking left permitting decisions to States or specified Title V applicability in addition to §63.11494(e).

checklist.item: Confirm whether the CMPU(s) at your facility contain any Table 1 HAP at concentrations meeting §63.11494(a)(2) thresholds (use SDS, formulation data, or testing).
Confirm that the CMPU is part of the facility-wide affected source (facility-wide collection of CMPUs, associated heat exchange systems, and wastewater systems).
Determine whether the control device is documented in a federally enforceable limitation (e.g., state/federal permit condition, consent decree, or other enforceable mechanism).

Determine whether, without the control device, the facility's emissions or potential to emit (considering design and limits) would equal or exceed major-source thresholds (10 tpy single HAP or 25 tpy combined).
If the control device makes you subject to Title V under §63.11494(e), determine when you became subject (on or before Dec 21, 2012, or after) to identify the permit application due date.
Check whether the Ohio Title V permitting authority has an exclusion or policy for area sources covered by this standard (i.e., whether the State exercised the option referenced in §63.1(c)(2)(i)).

candidates.title: Lead Acid Battery Manufacturing and Lead Acid Battery Component Manufacturing

gates.question: Is your facility a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant that is an area source of HAP emissions?
gates.test: yes -> consider Subpart PPPPPP; no -> Subpart PPPPPP does not apply
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant that is an area source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions.

gates.question: Are the new Humidity Curing and Drying Oven Chambers part of the plant-level affected source (i.e., are they lead-emitting operations associated with the lead acid battery manufacturing plant)?
gates.test: yes -> ovens are within the affected source; no -> ovens may not be covered by this affected-source definition
gates.quote: the affected source includes all grid casting facilities, paste mixing facilities, three-process operation facilities, lead oxide manufacturing facilities, lead reclamation facilities, and any other lead-emitting operation

gates.question: Is the plant classified as an area source (versus a major source) of HAPs for purposes of this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> area-source provisions apply; no -> different requirements may apply (not covered in provided text)
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant that is an area source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions.

gates.question: Is the affected source existing (construction/reconstruction commenced on or before April 4, 2007) or new (commenced after April 4, 2007)?
gates.test: yes (existing) -> existing-source provisions may allow use of prior performance tests; no (new) -> new-source provisions apply
gates.quote: A lead acid battery manufacturing plant affected source is existing if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or before April 4, 2007.

gates.question: Has a prior performance test been conducted on the same methods for these ovens and either no process changes occurred since that test, or can you demonstrate prior results reliably demonstrate compliance despite changes?
gates.test: yes -> initial performance test may not be required for existing sources; no -> initial performance test required
gates.quote: Existing sources are not required to conduct an initial performance test if a prior performance test was conducted using the same methods specified in this section

gates.question: Can the new ovens be grouped with existing similar affected sources (same process type and same type of air pollution control device) so testing a representative unit suffices for subsequent performance testing?
gates.test: yes -> you may test a representative affected source within the group (submit test plan); no -> each affected source must be tested separately
gates.quote: the affected sources that are grouped together must be of the same process type (e.g., grid casting, paste mixing, three-process operations) and also have the same type of air pollution control device (e.g., fabric filters).

gates.question: If the ovens are new, do they start up after February 23, 2022 (triggering the Feb 23, 2023 compliance timing) or earlier (different compliance dates may apply)?
gates.test: yes (start after Feb 23, 2022) -> comply by Feb 23, 2023 or upon startup; no -> earlier compliance deadlines may apply
gates.quote: If you start up a new lead acid battery manufacturing plant or lead acid battery component manufacturing plant affected source after February 23, 2022, you must achieve compliance with the applicable provisions in this subpart not later than February 23, 2023, or upon initial startup of your affected source, whichever is later.

missing: Whether the new oven chambers have had prior performance tests using the same methods referenced by this subpart
Whether any process changes have occurred at the ovens since any prior tests
Whether the new ovens are the same process type and use the same air pollution control device type as the existing ovens you propose to group with
Whether a prior waiver of performance testing was previously granted by the Administrator for the existing ovens

candidates.title: General Provisions (performance testing and waivers)

gates.question: Does a relevant standard require you to perform a performance test within 180 days of the compliance date for the affected source?
gates.test: yes -> performance test deadline typically within 180 days; no -> check relevant standard for other timing
gates.quote: the owner or operator of the affected source must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date for such source.

gates.question: Can you obtain a waiver of the performance test by written application showing the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis or otherwise qualifying for a waiver?
gates.test: yes -> Administrator may waive the individual performance test upon application; no -> you must perform the required test
gates.quote: Individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis

gates.question: If you apply for a waiver, will you submit the waiver application at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test (unless submitting a site-specific test plan)?
gates.test: yes -> meets the submission timing in §63.7(h)(3); no -> Administrator may still consider but timelines in §63.7 apply
gates.quote: the application for a waiver of an initial performance test shall be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if the site-specific test plan under paragraph (c) of this section is not submitted.

missing: Whether you have documented continuous compliance demonstrating the ovens meet the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis (for waiver justification)
Whether you previously received a written waiver from the Administrator and the scope/conditions of that waiver
Whether you will submit the waiver application at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test or with a site-specific test plan

candidates.title: Extensions, waivers, and alternatives (general waiver procedures)

gates.question: Has the owner/operator applied for a waiver of the performance test and can demonstrate to the Administrator that the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis or otherwise qualifies for waiver/extension?
gates.test: yes -> Administrator may grant waiver of performance tests; no -> performance testing required per relevant standard
gates.quote: Individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis, or the source is being operated under an extension of compliance, or the owner or operator has requested an extension of compliance and the Administrator is still considering that request.

gates.question: Will the waiver application be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if no site-specific test plan is submitted?
gates.test: yes -> meets the submittal timing in §63.1112(b)(3); no -> application may be considered but will not meet the specified timing
gates.quote: the application for a waiver of an initial performance test shall be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if a site-specific test plan is not submitted.

missing: Whether you have specifically applied to the Administrator (or delegated authority) for a waiver for the existing ovens and the outcome of that application
Documentation showing continuous compliance or other justification the Administrator would rely on to grant a waiver
Whether you plan to submit a site-specific test plan in lieu of a waiver application timing

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Combustion Turbines (Subpart YYYY)

gates.question: Is the turbine a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine as defined by this subpart?
gates.test: Yes -> This subpart's emission and operating limitations (Table 1 and Table 2) apply to this category; No -> This subpart's specific turbine provisions likely do not apply under this category.
gates.quote: For each new or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine which is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine, you must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart.

gates.question: Is the stationary combustion turbine not equipped with an oxidation catalyst?
gates.test: Yes -> You must petition the Administrator for operating limitations to monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde limitation (or petition for approval of no additional limits); No -> If equipped with an oxidation catalyst, monitor catalyst inlet temperature per the subpart.
gates.quote: If your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations that you will monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation in Table 1.

gates.question: Is the turbine located at a 'major source' (for example, for applying the distillate-oil monitoring requirements referenced in this subpart)?
gates.test: Yes -> Certain monitoring/recordkeeping requirements for turbines at the major source (e.g., distillate oil usage tracking) apply; No -> Those 'major source' specific monitoring requirements do not apply.
gates.quote: you must monitor and record your distillate oil usage daily for all new and existing stationary combustion turbines located at the major source with a non-resettable hour meter to measure the number of hours that distillate oil is fired.

gates.question: Is this turbine a 'new or reconstructed' stationary combustion turbine subject to the emission and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2?
gates.test: Yes -> The emission and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 (and associated monitoring/testing requirements) apply; No -> Different applicability or exemptions may apply and Tables may not apply.
gates.quote: For each new or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine which is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine, you must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart.

gates.question: Do you intend to petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations (or for approval of no additional operating limitations) to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation?
gates.test: Yes -> Your petition must include the information required in paragraph (f) and you must not conduct the initial performance test until the petition is decided; No -> You will follow the default/other monitoring requirements specified for turbines with or without catalysts.
gates.quote: (f) If you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation in Table 1, your petition must include the following information described in paragraphs (f)(1) through (5) of this section.

gates.question: Will you conduct the initial performance test (or other initial compliance demonstration) within 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.6095?
gates.test: Yes -> Initial performance test timing would meet the subpart's stated 180-day requirement; No -> The initial performance test would be late relative to the 180-day requirement (see notification and reporting provisions).
gates.quote: within 180 calendar days after the compliance date that is specified for your stationary combustion turbine in § 63.6095 and according to the provisions in § 63.7(a)(2).

Correlation data or guidance showing how %Load and inlet air temperature (T1) relate quantitatively to formaldehyde emissions (the petition must demonstrate this per § 63.6120(f)(2)).
Whether the turbine or the major source uses any distillate oil or other fuels that trigger the additional monitoring requirements in § 63.6125(c)-(d).

Plan to conduct the initial performance test within 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.6095, if applicable.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

gates.question: Does your facility own or operate an MSW landfill that has accepted waste since November 8, 1987 or has additional capacity for waste deposition?
gates.test: yes -> facility is in the universe addressed by Subpart AAAA and proceed to affected_source and major/area tests; no -> Subpart AAAA does not apply
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an MSW landfill that has accepted waste since November 8, 1987, or has additional capacity for waste deposition

gates.question: Is the affected source an MSW landfill (the entire contiguous disposal facility) that meets the criteria in §63.1935(a) or (b)?
gates.test: yes -> the entire landfill is an affected source under Subpart AAAA and proceed to threshold/operational tests; no -> Subpart AAAA does not apply to this facility
gates.quote: An affected source of this subpart is an MSW landfill, as defined in § 63.1990, that meets the criteria in § 63.1935(a) or (b).

gates.question: Is the landfill a major source, collocated with a major source, or an area source landfill with design capacity ≥ 2.5 million Mg and ≥ 2.5 million m3 with estimated uncontrolled NMOC emissions ≥ 50 Mg/yr?
gates.test: yes -> landfill meets one of the subjectivity criteria in §63.1935 and Subpart AAAA requirements apply; no -> landfill may not be subject under those criteria
gates.quote: meets any one of the three criteria in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section: (1) Your MSW landfill is a major source as defined in § 63.2 of subpart A.

gates.question: Does the landfill have a design capacity equal to or greater than 2.5 million Mg and 2.5 million m3?
gates.test: yes -> owner/operator must either follow active collection system requirements or calculate NMOC emission rate under §63.1959(b); no -> different reporting/requirements may apply
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of an affected source having a design capacity equal to or greater than 2.5 million Mg and 2.5 million m 3 must either comply with paragraph (b)(2) of this section or calculate an NMOC emission rate

gates.question: Does the landfill meet all removal/capping criteria in §63.1957(b) (i.e., closed landfill OR 15 years of operation (or demonstrated inability to operate 15 years) AND calculated NMOC < 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates 90–180 days apart)?
gates.test: yes -> collection and control system may be capped, removed, or decommissioned per §63.1957(b) (follow equipment removal/reporting requirements); no -> you may not decommission the collection and control system under §63.1957(b)
gates.quote: Following the procedures specified in § 63.1959(c), the calculated NMOC emission rate at the landfill is less than 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates.

gates.question: Will you submit an equipment removal report to the Administrator at least 30 days prior to removal or cessation of operation of the control equipment?
gates.test: yes -> follows the notification timing required by §63.1981(g)(1); no -> failing to submit the required equipment removal report at least 30 days prior would not meet §63.1981(g)(1)
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of a controlled landfill must submit an equipment removal report to the Administrator 30 days prior to removal or cessation of operation of the control equipment.

gates.question: Is the planned action to decommission a single well (versus capping/removing the collection and control system) such that it constitutes a design change requiring Administrator approval?
gates.test: yes -> decommissioning a well may be a design change that must be approved by the Administrator as specified in §63.1981(d)(2); no -> if removing the full system, follow §63.1957 removal criteria and equipment removal report requirements
gates.quote: A well may experience a static positive pressure after shut down to accommodate for declining flows. All design changes must be approved by the Administrator as specified in § 63.1981(d)(2);

missing: Whether the landfill is permanently closed (closure report) or remains active.
The NMOC emission rate values and dates for three successive tests (90–180 days apart) to demonstrate < 50 Mg/yr as required by §63.1957(b)(3).

Date the gas collection and control system (or the common-header system) was placed in operation (to determine if it has operated a minimum of 15 years) or documentation demonstrating inability to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow.
Whether proposed decommissioning is for an individual well (EW-308A) versus capping/removing the entire collection and control system.
Whether the landfill currently has a collection and control system in operation and whether it is a 'controlled landfill' per definitions.
Whether an equipment removal report will be submitted at least 30 days prior to removal and whether a closure report has been or will be submitted.
Measured or estimated NMOC emissions (Tier 1/2/3 inputs) and design capacity documentation used to determine applicability (e.g., permit showing 5.9 million Mg).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

gates.question: Is the landfill a 'major source' as defined in §63.2 of subpart A (or collocated with a major source)?
gates.test: yes -> the landfill meets one of the criteria in §63.1935 and Subpart AAAA may apply as a major source; no -> evaluate area-source criteria (design capacity and NMOC emissions) under Subpart AAAA
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an MSW landfill that has accepted waste since November 8, 1987, or has additional capacity for waste deposition and meets any one of the three criteria in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section:

missing: Documentation to determine whether the landfill qualifies as a 'major source' under §63.2 (e.g., facility-level potential to emit HAPs or known collocation with a major source).
If not a major source, the area-source NMOC emissions estimate and design capacity for Subpart AAAA applicability.

checklist.item: Confirm whether the landfill accepted waste since November 8, 1987 or has additional capacity for waste deposition.
Provide documentation of the landfill's design capacity in megagrams (Mg) and cubic meters (m3) (permit or engineering calculation).
Provide whether the landfill is currently closed and date of closure (and copy of closure report if closed).

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products

gates.question: Is your facility a plywood and composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility with an affected source?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart DDDD applies to the affected source at your facility; no -> Subpart DDDD does not apply to this facility
gates.quote: The affected source is the collection of dryers, refiners, blenders, formers, presses, board coolers, and other process units associated with the manufacturing of plywood and composite wood products.

gates.question: Does your equipment include a reconstituted wood product press and/or a reconstituted wood product board cooler (as defined in this subpart)?
gates.test: yes -> those pieces of equipment are process units subject to the compliance options in this subpart; no -> those specific definitions do not apply
gates.quote: Reconstituted wood product board cooler means a piece of equipment designed to reduce the temperature of a board by means of forced air or convection within a controlled time period after the board exits the reconstituted wood product press unloader.

gates.question: Is the affected source a major source of HAP (or did an area source become a major source)?
gates.test: yes -> major-source compliance timing and obligations apply; no -> area-source status (or existing applicable deadlines) applies
gates.quote: you must be in compliance with this subpart by October 1, 2007 or upon initial startup of your affected source as a major source

gates.question: If you choose a concentration-based control-system compliance option for a control system outlet from a reconstituted press or a new board cooler, does the capture device meet the wood products enclosure definition or achieve ≥95% capture efficiency?

gates.test: Yes -> proceed to major-source threshold gate; No -> this affected-source definition may not apply

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of HAPs (any single HAP ≥ 9.07 megagrams (10 tons)/yr or any combination of HAPs ≥ 22.68 megagrams (25 tons)/yr)?
gates.test: Yes -> this subpart can apply to the facility (if other gates met); No -> if area source, subpart applies only if it later becomes a major source per rules

gates.question: Does your affected source meet an exemption in § 63.5981(b) (primary product already subject to another subpart, or a research and development facility not manufacturing products for commercial sale)?

gates.quote: Your rubber tire manufacturing affected source is a research and development facility whose primary purpose is to conduct research and development into new processes and products, where such source is operated under the close supervision of technically trained personnel

gates.question: If this is an existing affected source, is it already meeting the emission limitations required for existing sources?
gates.test: Yes -> must maintain compliance (existing-source requirements apply); No -> must come into compliance no later than the existing-source date
gates.quote: If you have an existing affected source, you must comply with the emission limitations for existing sources no later than July 11, 2005.

Whether the facility is a research and development facility as defined/exempted under §63.5981(b)(2)

gates.quote: (ii) Install and operate a continuous gas analyzer to measure and record the concentration of carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and oxygen of the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust.

candidates.title: Aerospace Manufacturing and Rework Operations

gates.question: Does the facility produce, rework, or repair aerospace vehicles or components and therefore fall within the aerospace manufacturing/rework source category?
gates.test: Yes -> the facility is within the aerospace source category for this NESHAP; No -> this subpart GG source category does not apply
gates.quote: This subpart applies to facilities that are engaged, either in part or in whole, in the manufacture or rework of commercial, civil, or military aerospace vehicles or components and that are major sources as defined in § 63.2.

gates.question: Do you perform hand-wipe, spray gun, or flush cleaning operations at the facility (each of which is listed as an affected source)?
gates.test: Yes -> those cleaning operations are affected sources under this subpart; No -> those cleaning operation categories are not affected sources
gates.quote: All hand-wipe cleaning operations constitute an affected source. (ii) Each spray gun cleaning operation constitutes an affected source. (iii) All flush cleaning operations constitute an affected source.

gates.question: Is the facility a major source as defined in § 63.2 (i.e., meets the major source threshold)?
gates.test: Yes -> Subpart GG applies only to major sources; No -> Subpart GG does not apply (facility is not a major source)
gates.quote: This subpart applies to facilities that are engaged, either in part or in whole, in the manufacture or rework of commercial, civil, or military aerospace vehicles or components and that are major sources as defined in § 63.2.

gates.question: For hand-wipe cleaning, does the cleaning solvent meet a Table 1 composition requirement, or have a composite vapor pressure of 45 mm Hg or less at 20 °C, or is there an approved 60% reduction plan?
gates.test: Yes -> the hand-wipe solvent meets one of the allowed thresholds/alternatives; No -> the hand-wipe solvent does not meet the composition/vapor-pressure/usage-reduction thresholds and must comply with other requirements
gates.quote: (1) Meet one of the composition requirements in Table 1 of this section; (2) Have a composite vapor pressure of 45 mm Hg (24.1 in. H2 O) or less at 20 °C (68 °F);

gates.question: Are the cleaning activities performed among the exemptions listed (for example, cleaning of electronic parts and assemblies or cleaning of aircraft fluid systems exposed to the fluid)?
gates.test: Yes -> those cleaning activities are exempt from the hand-wipe/spray/flush requirements in §63.744(b); No -> the cleaning activities are not exempt and the standards apply
gates.quote: (4) Cleaning of electronic parts and assemblies containing electronic parts; (5) Cleaning of aircraft and ground support equipment fluid systems that are exposed to the fluid, including air-to-air heat exchangers and hydraulic fluid systems;

gates.question: Is this an existing affected source (subject to the existing-source compliance date) or a new source (subject to new-source timing)?
gates.test: Yes (existing) -> must comply by the existing-source compliance date; No (new) -> must comply on effective date or upon startup, whichever is later
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of an existing affected source subject to this subpart shall comply with the requirements of this subpart by September 1, 1998, ...

gates.question: Do the solvents used meet the definition of 'non-HAP material' such that primers/topcoats/cleaning solvents defined as non-HAP are not regulated?
gates.test: Yes -> materials defined as non-HAP are not regulated under this subpart (but recordkeeping may apply if included in averaging); No -> the materials remain regulated
gates.quote: The requirements of this subpart do not apply to primers, topcoats, specialty coatings, chemical milling maskants, strippers, and cleaning solvents that meet the definition of non-HAP material, as determined from manufacturer's representations, such as in a material safety data sheet or product data sheet, or testing,

missing: Whether the facility qualifies as a major source (tons/year of HAP emissions) under § 63.2

Which specific cleaning operations are performed on-site (hand-wipe, spray-gun, flush) and the parts being cleaned (electronic assemblies vs completed assemblies; aircraft fluid systems vs unrelated parts)
The exact identity, formulation, HAP content, and composite vapor pressure of the solvents used (to determine Table 1 composition, non-HAP status, or the <=45 mm Hg vapor-pressure test)
Annual or monthly volumes of each cleaning solvent used (for possible averaging, thresholds, or the 60% reduction alternative)
Whether any cleaning of electronic assemblies involves 'completed assemblies' or topcoating (which may change applicability)

candidates.title: General Provisions (applicable parts referenced by Subpart GG)

gates.question: Are the Subpart A General Provisions (e.g., §§ 63.4, 63.5, 63.6) applicable to your affected source as incorporated by Subpart GG?
gates.test: Yes -> comply with the cited Subpart A requirements (notification, compliance, prohibited activities); No -> Subpart A provisions do not apply (rare if GG applies)
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of an affected source subject to this subpart is also subject to the following sections of subpart A of this part: (1) § 63.4, Prohibited activities and circumvention;

gates.question: If seeking an extension of compliance under Subpart A provisions as applied in GG, was any extension request submitted at least 120 days before the affected source's compliance date?
gates.test: Yes -> extension request timing requirement satisfied; No -> extension request may be untimely under the subpart-specific rule
gates.quote: For the purposes of this subpart, all affected sources shall submit any request for an extension of compliance not later than 120 days before the affected source's compliance date.

checklist.item: List all cleaning operation types performed (hand-wipe, spray gun, flush) and indicate which operations are used to clean electronic assemblies or aircraft fluid systems (hydraulic fluid).
Provide the exact solvent product names, manufacturer data sheets (MSDS/PDS), HAP constituents, and composite vapor pressures for each solvent used in hand-wipe, spray-gun, and flush cleaning.
Report monthly and annual volumes of each cleaning solvent used (to evaluate averaging, de minimis, and the 60% reduction alternative).
Confirm facility classification as major or area source (tons/year of HAP emissions) per § 63.2.

candidates.title: Petroleum Refinery Sector (Subpart CC)

gates.question: Is this emission point part of a petroleum refining process unit at your plant site?
gates.test: yes -> proceed to determine whether subpart CC applies; no -> subpart CC likely does not apply
gates.quote: This subpart applies to petroleum refining process units and to related emissions points that are specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (9) of this section

gates.question: Is the orthoxylene rerun column vent a miscellaneous process vent (i.e., a gas stream containing >20 ppmv organic HAP) from a petroleum refining process unit?
gates.test: yes -> the vent is an affected miscellaneous process vent under subpart CC; no -> this subpart's miscellaneous process vent requirements may not apply
gates.quote: Miscellaneous process vent means a gas stream containing greater than 20 parts per million by volume organic HAP that is continuously or periodically discharged from a petroleum refining process unit meeting the criteria specified in § 63.640(a).

gates.question: Is the plant site a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act?
gates.test: yes -> the affected-source definition in §63.640 applies; no -> subpart CC would not apply (area sources are not subject to subpart CC)
gates.quote: Are located at a plant site that is a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act;

gates.question: Do you propose to control the vent by achieving a 98 weight-percent reduction of organic HAP or to an outlet concentration of 20 ppmv (dry, corrected to 3% O2), whichever is less stringent?
gates.test: yes -> this meets the reference control technology option in §63.643(a)(2); no -> other compliance options (e.g., flare per §63.643(a)(1)) or different monitoring approaches apply
gates.quote: Reduce emissions of organic HAP's, using a control device, by 98 weight-percent or to a concentration of 20 parts per million by volume, on a dry basis, corrected to 3 percent oxygen, whichever is less stringent.

gates.question: Is the vent used only as a maintenance vent (used solely during startup, shutdown, maintenance, or inspection) such that maintenance-vent provisions apply instead?
gates.test: yes -> the vent may be treated as a maintenance vent and subject only to the maintenance-vent provisions; no -> normal Group 1 miscellaneous process vent requirements apply
gates.quote: An owner or operator may designate a process vent as a maintenance vent if the vent is only used as a result of startup, shutdown, maintenance, or inspection of equipment where equipment is emptied, depressurized, degassed or placed into service.

gates.question: Do you intend to request EPA approval to monitor parameters other than those listed for the control device (i.e., revise the alternative monitoring plan)?
gates.test: yes -> submit a request per §63.655(h) as allowed by §63.644(b); no -> follow the monitoring parameters listed in §63.644(a) for the specific control device
gates.quote: An owner or operator of a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent may request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) of this section.

missing: Whether the orthoxylene rerun column vent meets the Group 1 emission-rate/TOC thresholds (e.g., total VOC emissions in kg/day) at the outlet of any recovery device
Whether the vent stream is currently routed to a flare, incinerator, boiler/process heater, or other control device and which device specifics apply
Measured or calculated organic HAP concentration and mass emission rates for the vent (to show Group 1 status and to demonstrate % reduction or 20 ppmv outlet)
Whether the vent is designated as a maintenance vent at your facility (and records supporting that designation)
Whether you will request approval to monitor parameters other than those specified and whether a site-specific test plan/performance data are available

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Process Vents (Subpart G)

gates.question: Is this emission point regulated under Subpart G as a Group 1 or Group 2 process vent?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart G process vent provisions may apply; no -> Subpart G does not apply
gates.quote: The owner or operator of a Group 1 process vent as defined in this subpart shall comply with the requirements of paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section, and paragraph (a)(5) of this section.

gates.question: Do you propose to meet the Subpart G reference control technology by reducing total organic HAP by 98 weight-percent or to an outlet concentration of 20 ppmv?
gates.test: yes -> this aligns with the Subpart G reference control technology option in §63.113(a)(2); no -> other Subpart G alternatives (TRE, recovery devices, etc.) may apply
gates.quote: Reduce emissions of total organic hazardous air pollutants by 98 weight-percent or to a concentration of 20 parts per million by volume.

gates.question: Does the vent contain halogenated vent streams (chlorinated compounds) that would preclude routing to a flare without halogen reduction?
gates.test: yes -> halogenated streams cannot be vented to a flare and additional halogen reduction (e.g., scrubber) is required; no -> flaring or the 98%/20 ppm option may be used as allowed
gates.quote: Halogenated vent streams, as defined in § 63.111, shall not be vented to a flare.

gates.question: Is the vent subject to the Subpart G maintenance-vent provisions (i.e., used only for startup/shutdown/maintenance/inspection) and the associated alternatives for deinventory before venting?
gates.test: yes -> maintenance-vent provisions and limits in §63.113(k) apply; no -> standard Group 1/Group 2 requirements apply
gates.quote: an owner or operator may designate a process vent as a maintenance vent if the vent is only used as a result of startup, shutdown, maintenance, or inspection of equipment where equipment is emptied, depressurized, degassed, or placed into service.

gates.question: Would you request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in §63.114 for the control device (i.e., submit alternative monitoring request)?
gates.test: yes -> submit request per the procedures referenced in §63.114(c); no -> monitor the parameters specified in §63.114 for the device
gates.quote: An owner or operator of a process vent may request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) or (b) of this section.

gates.question: Do you have performance data or a test plan to support any requested alternative monitoring or alternative emission limits under Subpart G?
gates.test: yes -> submit test plan/results per Subpart G procedures; no -> must follow prescribed monitoring and control requirements until such approval is granted
gates.quote: Where an incinerator is used, a temperature monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder is required.

missing: Whether the vent is part of a chemical manufacturing process unit subject to Subpart G (process classification) versus a petroleum refinery process unit (Subpart CC)
Whether the vent stream contains halogenated compounds or ethylene oxide (which impose additional Subpart G requirements)
Measured vent flow rate, TRE index (if applicable), and HAP concentrations to determine Group 1 vs Group 2 applicability under Subpart G
Existing monitoring parameters and any prior performance tests relevant to establishing monitoring ranges or alternative monitoring

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

gates.question: Are you requesting Administrator approval to use an alternative means of emission limitation or alternative monitoring in lieu of the promulgated standard?
gates.test: yes -> §63.6(g) provides the Administrator may permit an alternative emission standard after public notice and comment; no -> follow the promulgated standard and subpart-specific procedures
gates.quote: the Administrator will publish in the Federal Register a notice permitting the use of the alternative emission standard for purposes of compliance with the promulgated standard.

gates.question: Can you submit the required test plan, monitoring results, and QA/QC (per §63.7/§63.8) to demonstrate equivalent or better HAP reduction as required by §63.6(g)(2)?
gates.test: yes -> include proposed test plan or results per §63.6(g)(2) to support request; no -> you must perform testing/monitoring to support any request
gates.quote: An owner or operator requesting permission under this paragraph shall, unless otherwise specified in an applicable subpart, submit a proposed test plan or the results of testing and monitoring in accordance with § 63.7 and § 63.8.

gates.question: Are you prepared to follow the public-notice and EPA approval steps (including any required test-plan approval and documentation) before an alternative is allowed for compliance purposes?
gates.test: yes -> EPA will publish notice and condition permission on assurance of proper operation and QA/QC; no -> cannot rely on an alternative until EPA approval and public process are completed
gates.quote: Any Federal Register notice under this paragraph shall be published only after the public is notified and given the opportunity to comment.

missing: Whether you have prepared and documented a site-specific performance test plan and QA/QC sufficient to demonstrate that the proposed alternative monitoring/limits achieve equivalent or better reductions than the applicable standard
Whether you have identified the exact alternative operating parameters, testing protocol, and quality assurance procedures to submit with the request
Whether you will follow any subpart-specific submission procedures (e.g., subpart CC §63.655(h) for miscellaneous process vents) in addition to §63.6(g) submission requirements

checklist.item: Verify vent meets Group 1 miscellaneous process vent criteria (>20 ppmv organic HAP and applicable VOC emission thresholds) and identify current control device.
Assemble or schedule performance testing (or provide existing test data) showing that the proposed control achieves >=98% reduction or <=20 ppmv outlet (dry, corrected to 3% O2).
If proposing alternative monitoring, prepare a site-specific monitoring/test plan (QA/QC) and be ready to submit per the applicable subpart procedures (Subpart CC §63.655(h) and Subpart A §63.6(g)).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Iron and Steel Foundries

gates.question: Is your facility an iron and steel foundry covered by this NESHAP?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart applies to your facility category; no -> this subpart does not apply on the basis of facility category
gates.quote: This subpart covers emissions from metal melting furnaces, scrap preheaters, pouring areas, pouring stations, automated conveyor and pallet cooling lines, automated shakeout lines, and mold and core making lines.

gates.question: Is the unit you tested (M-1 Pouring Area) a pouring area or pouring station at your foundry?
gates.test: yes -> the tested unit is a regulated emissions source under this subpart; no -> the tested unit is not a regulated emissions source under this subpart
gates.quote: This subpart covers emissions from metal melting furnaces, scrap preheaters, pouring areas, pouring stations, automated conveyor and pallet cooling lines, automated shakeout lines, and mold and core making lines.

gates.question: Is the affected source an "existing" source (construction or reconstruction commenced before December 23, 2002)?
gates.test: yes -> the source is treated as an existing affected source; no -> the source is treated as new (or reconstructed) under this subpart
gates.quote: The affected source is each new or existing iron and steel foundry. An affected source is existing if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before December 23, 2002.

gates.question: Was the performance test conducted under conditions representative of normal operations (excluding startup/shutdown) with recorded process information and an explanation supporting representativeness?
gates.test: yes -> the test meets the representativeness requirement for initial compliance demonstration; no -> the test may not be acceptable as an initial compliance demonstration
gates.quote: Each performance test must be conducted under conditions representative of normal operations. Normal operating conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown.

gates.question: Did each PM sampling run collect at least 60 dscf and were a minimum of three valid test runs obtained?
gates.test: yes -> the test meets the minimum sampling volume and run count requirements; no -> the test does not meet minimum test-run or sample-volume criteria
gates.quote: Collect a minimum sample volume of 60 dscf of gas during each PM sampling run. A minimum of three valid test runs are needed to comprise a performance test.

gates.question: Did you submit a notification of intent to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the test was scheduled?
gates.test: yes -> the required pre-test notification timing was met; no -> the pre-test notification requirement was not met, which may affect acceptance
gates.quote: If you are required to conduct a performance test, you must submit a notification of intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin as required by § 63.7(b)(1).

gates.question: Was the performance test conducted no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.7683?
gates.test: yes -> the test was within the 180-day window after the compliance date; no -> the test was not within that 180-day window (it may have been earlier or later)
gates.quote: you must conduct a performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date that is specified in § 63.7683

gates.question: Did you submit the notification of compliance status, including the performance test results, within 60 calendar days after completion of the performance test?
gates.test: yes -> the post-test notification timing requirement was met; no -> the post-test notification requirement was not met
gates.quote: you must submit the notification of compliance status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Mercury

gates.question: Is the unit a mercury thermal recovery unit vent at a mercury recovery facility?
gates.test: yes -> consider mercury thermal recovery unit provisions under Subpart IIIII; no -> Subpart IIIII mercury recovery-unit provisions do not apply
gates.quote: New, reconstructed, or existing mercury recovery facility. You must not discharge to the atmosphere mercury emissions in excess of the applicable limit in paragraph (a)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section.

gates.question: Are you using the continuous monitoring option (a mercury CEMS) under § 63.8240(a) for the mercury thermal recovery unit vent?
gates.test: yes -> follow continuous-monitoring compliance procedures (daily-average from 15-minute readings); no -> follow periodic monitoring procedures in § 63.8240(b) (use test-run averaging)
gates.quote: You must continuously monitor the mercury concentration using a mercury continuous emissions monitor according to the requirements in §§ 63.8242(a) and 63.8244(a);

gates.question: If you choose continuous monitoring, must you calculate a daily-average mercury concentration to demonstrate compliance?
gates.test: yes -> calculate daily average using 15-minute CEMS readings per the continuous option; no -> if periodic option chosen, use procedures in § 63.8234(b) to calculate daily averages from test runs
gates.quote: If you choose the continuous monitoring option in § 63.8240(a), you must demonstrate continuous compliance using paragraph (b)(1) of this section. If you choose the periodic monitoring option in § 63.8240(b), you must demonstrate continuous compliance using paragraph (b)(2) of this section.

gates.question: Have you begun collecting required monitoring data starting on the compliance date specified for your affected source?
gates.test: yes -> data collection start aligns with compliance-date requirements; no -> you must begin collecting data on the compliance date in § 63.8186 before calculating averages
gates.quote: You must begin collecting data on the compliance date that is specified in § 63.8186 for your affected source and calculate your first 52-week average mercury emission rate at the end of the 52nd week after the compliance date.

missing: Whether this specific unit is a mercury thermal recovery unit vent (facility/vent type)
Which monitoring option has been chosen for this vent (continuous CEMS or periodic testing)
Whether a mercury continuous emissions monitor (Hg CEMS) is installed and operating
The applicable compliance date for this affected source per § 63.8186

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (EGUs context for Hg averaging)

gates.question: Are you using a CEMS or sorbent-trap system to measure Hg emissions for an affected unit covered by this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart UUUUU hourly-data rolling-average procedures for Hg may apply; no -> this subpart's CEMS-based rolling-average procedures for Hg do not apply
gates.quote: you must demonstrate continuous compliance by using all quality-assured hourly data recorded by the CEMS (or sorbent trap monitoring system) and the other required monitoring systems to calculate the arithmetic average emissions rate

gates.question: Do you plan to calculate Hg compliance using hourly CEMS (or sorbent trap) data on a multi-day rolling average?
gates.test: yes -> use the 30-boiler operating day rolling average (or 90-day alternative for Hg) updated at end of each operating day; no -> alternate (e.g., quarterly performance testing) approaches may apply
gates.quote: on a continuous 30-boiler operating day (or, if alternate emissions averaging is used for Hg, 90-boiler operating day) rolling average basis, updated at the end of each new boiler operating day.

gates.question: Will you use hourly emissions-rate values (Heri) to compute the arithmetic rolling average per Equation 8?
gates.test: yes -> compute arithmetic average using all quality-assured hourly Heri values over the 30- or 90-boiler operating day window; no -> you are not using hourly-data rolling-average method
gates.quote: Where: Heri is the hourly emissions rate for hour i and n is the number of hourly emissions rate values collected over 30- (or, if applicable, 90-) boiler operating days.

missing: Whether the affected unit at the facility is within the source category covered by Subpart UUUUU (an EGU/boiler subject to these tables)
Whether a Hg CEMS or sorbent trap monitoring system is actually in use
Whether the facility will use the 30-day or 90-day rolling averaging option for Hg (if an alternate averaging approach is elected)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Copper Smelting and Related Operations (includes mercury provisions)

gates.question: Is your affected source subject to the mercury emissions limit in § 63.1444 and therefore covered by the continuous-compliance mercury provisions in this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart QQQ mercury continuous-compliance requirements (Hg CEMS, 6-hour average) may apply; no -> Subpart QQQ mercury provisions do not apply
gates.quote: Maintain the average concentration of mercury discharged from the facility at or below the emission limit in § 63.1444 monitored by a mercury continuous emissions monitoring system (Hg CEMS).

gates.question: Are you using an Hg CEMS to demonstrate continuous compliance for mercury under this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> you must install/operate Hg CEMS per PS 12A and follow the 6-hour rolling-average requirement; no -> you must monitor operating parameters and perform annual performance tests per the subpart
gates.quote: If the Hg CEMS is used, you must demonstrate continuous compliance according to the requirements in paragraphs (g)(1)(i) through (v) of this section. (iv) Determine the average on a 6-hour rolling basis.

gates.question: If you use an Hg CEMS, have you installed and are you operating it according to Performance Specification 12A (PS 12A)?
gates.test: yes -> CEMS installation/operation per PS 12A supports use of the 6-hour rolling-average compliance calculation; no -> you cannot rely on Hg CEMS averaging under these provisions until PS 12A requirements are met
gates.quote: Install and operate a Hg CEMS in accordance with Performance Specification 12A (PS 12A) of appendix B to 40 CFR part 60.

checklist.item: Confirm whether the unit is a mercury thermal recovery unit vent (mercury recovery facility vs. other mercury source).
Confirm whether you will use continuous mercury monitoring (Hg CEMS) or periodic test-run monitoring for the unit.
If using Hg CEMS, confirm the monitoring system meets the applicable performance/specification requirements (e.g., § 63.8242 for Subpart IIIII or PS 12A for Subpart QQQ).

checklist.item: Confirm whether glucosamine hydrochloride produced at the facility is intended as a pharmaceutical active ingredient or pharmaceutical product (SIC 2833/2834 or NAICS 325411/325412).
