Confirm whether the process unit meets the MCPU definition (equipment, storage tanks, and components assigned to an MCPU).
Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAP (plant-wide potential or actual emissions: >=10 tpy single HAP or >=25 tpy total HAP).
Confirm whether the facility actually produces liquid HCl product (and if so, its concentration) or only uses hydrochloric acid as a reagent.
Verify whether any HCl production, if present, is subject to another NESHAP (e.g., Subpart GGG) that would exempt it from Subpart NNNNN.

candidates.title: Site Remediation (National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants)

gates.question: Does your activity meet the definition of site remediation in § 63.7957 (i.e., activities used to remove, destroy, degrade, transform, immobilize, or otherwise manage remediation material)?
gates.test: yes -> activity is a 'site remediation' under the rule; no -> activity is not a site remediation under the rule
gates.quote: Site remediation means one or more activities or processes used to remove, destroy, degrade, transform, immobilize, or otherwise manage remediation material.

gates.question: Does the excavation, temporary on-site storage, or reuse as backfill involve any affected source types (process vents, remediation material management units, equipment in remediation material service, or pressure relief devices) listed in § 63.7882(a)(1)-(4)?
gates.test: yes -> the activity involves one or more affected source types covered by the subpart; no -> the activity does not involve those affected source types
gates.quote: This subpart applies to each new, reconstructed, or existing affected source for your Site Remediation as designated by paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section.

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of HAP (i.e., emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/year combined)?
gates.test: yes -> facility meets the major source thresholds referenced by the subpart; no -> facility does not meet the major source thresholds
gates.quote: A major source emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at the rate of 10 tons (9.07 megagrams) or more per year.

gates.question: Is the total annual quantity of HAP in the remediation material placed in the remediation material management units you might claim exempt less than 1 megagram (1 Mg/yr)?
gates.test: yes -> total annual HAP in the exempted remediation material management units is <1 Mg/yr; no -> total annual HAP in those units is ≥1 Mg/yr
gates.quote: the total annual quantity of HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart contained in the remediation material placed in all of the remediation material management units exempted under this paragraph is less than 1 Mg/yr.

gates.question: Will the site remediation be completed within 30 consecutive calendar days, per the conditions in § 63.7884(b)?
gates.test: yes -> the remediation may qualify for the 30-day exemption from the standards; no -> the 30-day exemption does not apply
gates.quote: A site remediation that is completed within 30 consecutive calendar days according to the conditions in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section is not subject to the standards under paragraph (a) of this section.

gates.question: Was the initial startup of the affected source (or the remediation activity) after September 3, 2019?
gates.test: yes -> initial startup after Sept 3, 2019 (compliance timing per the later dates in § 63.7935(a)); no -> initial startup on or before Sept 3, 2019 (different timing/exceptions may apply)
gates.quote: If your initial startup was after September 3, 2019, then as of July 10, 2020, and for all sources, after January 6, 2021, you must be in compliance

missing: Whether the excavated soil contains any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG (VOHAP / speciated HAP concentrations).
Whether the remediation activity is co-located with one or more other stationary sources at the facility that emit HAP (required by § 63.7881(a)(2)).
The facility's HAP emissions inventory or determination of major source status (single/combined HAP tonnage).

Whether the excavated soil will be managed in units that qualify as remediation material management units (tanks, containers, surface impoundments, separators, transfer systems) per § 63.7957 and § 63.7882.

The total annual quantity of HAP (Table 1) that will be placed in any remediation material management units or otherwise handled—needed to evaluate the 1 Mg exemptions in § 63.7881(c) and § 63.7886(d).
Whether the remediation will be completed within the 30 consecutive calendar day exemption conditions (dates of initiation and completion, and whether shipping off-site or staged activities apply).
Initial startup date of the affected source or remediation activity to determine applicable compliance timelines under § 63.7935.

checklist.item: Is the work removing or otherwise managing soil that contains HAP (i.e., does the activity meet the § 63.7957 definition of site remediation)?

Will you temporarily store the excavated soil in tanks, containers, surface impoundments, transfer systems, or otherwise use equipment that contacts remediation material (process vents, equipment in remediation material service, pressure relief devices)?
Does the facility emit or have the potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/year combined HAP (facility major source determination)?
Is the total annual quantity of Table 1 HAP in remediation material placed in the units you might claim exempt less than 1 Mg/year?
Will the entire remediation be initiated and completed within 30 consecutive calendar days (and meet the shipment/documentation conditions if material is sent off-site)?
Was the initial startup of the affected source (or remediation activity) after September 3, 2019?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Organic Liquid Distribution (Non-Gasoline) Operations

gates.question: Is your organic liquids distribution operation located at, or part of, a major source of HAP emissions?
gates.test: yes -> EEEE may apply; no -> EEEE does not apply
gates.quote: Except as provided for in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, you are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an OLD operation that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP emissions.

gates.question: Are the transfers performed at or using transfer racks, storage tanks, transport vehicles, or containers that are part of the affected source at the plant?
gates.test: yes -> those transfer/containers are part of the affected source under EEEE; no -> those activities may be outside the affected source
gates.quote: The affected source is composed of: (1) All storage tanks storing organic liquids. (2) All transfer racks at which organic liquids are loaded into or unloaded out of transport vehicles and/or containers.

gates.question: Are the transfers performed at equipment that meets the definition of a transfer rack (a system used to load into or unload out of transport vehicles or containers)?
gates.test: yes -> the operation fits the transfer rack definition in EEEE; no -> may not be a transfer rack subject to EEEE
gates.quote: Transfer rack means a single system used to load organic liquids into, or unload organic liquids out of, transport vehicles or containers.

gates.question: Does the collection of transfer racks at the facility meet the total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume criterion for control in Table 2 (items 7 through 10)?
gates.test: yes -> transfer-rack control provisions in §63.2346(b) apply; no -> transfer-rack control provisions may not apply
gates.quote: For each transfer rack that is part of the collection of transfer racks that meets the total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume criterion for control in Table 2 to this subpart, items 7 through 10,

gates.question: Are the non-permanent transfer equipment, containers, or hoses/valves used only in special situation distribution loading and unloading operations (such as maintenance or upset liquids management)?
gates.test: yes -> non-permanent items used only in special situations are excluded from the affected source; no -> they are not excluded and may be subject
gates.quote: Non-permanent storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, and equipment leak components when used in special situation distribution loading and unloading operations (such as maintenance or upset liquids management).

gates.question: Is the affected source an existing affected source (not new or reconstructed)?
gates.test: yes -> compliance schedule for existing sources applies (see §63.2342(b)); no -> new/reconstructed schedule applies (see §63.2342(a))
gates.quote: If you have an existing affected source, you must comply with the emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards for existing affected sources no later than February 5, 2007.

missing: Whether the facility is a major source of HAP emissions (plant-level status).
Whether these specific container-to-container and truck-to-container transfers occur at transfer racks or otherwise within the affected source as defined
Whether the hoses/valves in use are non-permanent and whether they are used only for special situations (maintenance/upset) or used routinely
The facility's total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume (3-year rolling average) to compare to Table 2 thresholds for transfer racks (items 7-10).
Whether the liquids transferred meet the definition of 'organic liquid' under this subpart (e.g., ≥5% Table 1 organic HAP, or crude/condensate).
Whether the transfers are only unloading (which may change applicability per §63.2343(a)) or include loading into containers/transport vehicles.

candidates.title: Referenced control and monitoring requirements (subpart SS) for storage tanks and transfer racks

gates.question: If your storage tanks or transfer racks are subject to control under EEEE, will you meet the emission limits by complying with the applicable requirements specified in subpart SS?
gates.test: yes -> compliance may be demonstrated by meeting subpart SS requirements; no -> other compliance options in EEEE (e.g., routing to fuel gas, vapor balancing, other controls) may be used
gates.quote: Meet the emission limits specified in Table 2 or 2b to this subpart and comply with paragraph (l) of this section and the applicable requirements specified in subpart SS of this part, for meeting emission limits.

missing: Whether the owner/operator intends to use subpart SS requirements to meet the EEEE emission limits (i.e., selection of control strategy).
Specific control device type, monitored parameters, and operating limits (subpart SS details are not included in the provided sections).

candidates.title: Referenced equipment leak control (subpart TT / control level 1)

gates.question: Do pumps, valves, or sampling connections operate in organic liquids service at least 300 hours per year?
gates.test: yes -> equipment leak requirements under referenced subparts (e.g., TT/UU/H) apply; no -> those components may not be subject to the component monitoring work practice
gates.quote: For each pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year, you must comply with paragraph (l) of this section and the applicable requirements under subpart TT of this part (control level 1), subpart UU of this part (control level 2), or subpart H of this part.

missing: Which equipment leak control level (TT, UU, or H) applies at this facility (depends on chosen/required control level).
Whether each specific pump, valve, or sampling connector is in 'organic liquids service' (≥5% Table 1 organic HAP) and its annual operating hours.

candidates.title: Referenced equipment leak control (subpart UU / control level 2)

gates.question: Are the equipment leak components (pumps, valves, sampling connections) in organic liquids service and subject to the equipment-leak provisions (operate ≥300 hours/year) that would trigger subpart UU or another referenced leak-control subpart?
gates.test: yes -> subpart UU (or TT/H as applicable) requirements will be implicated; no -> equipment-leak work practice requirements may not apply
gates.quote: For each pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year, you must comply with paragraph (l) of this section and the applicable requirements under subpart TT of this part (control level 1), subpart UU of this part (control level 2), or subpart H of this part.

missing: Whether subpart UU (control level 2) is the selected/required equipment-leak standard for the affected source.
Component-level information: identities, service (organic liquid fraction), and annual hours of operation.

checklist.item: Is the plant a major source of HAP emissions (plant-level determination)?
Do these transfers occur at transfer racks—or otherwise as loading/unloading into/out of containers or transport vehicles within the affected source?
Are the hoses/valves in these transfers non-permanent and used only during special situations (maintenance, upset liquids management) or used routinely?
What is the facility's total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume through transfer racks (3-year rolling average)?
Do the fluids transferred meet the subpart's 'organic liquid' definition (e.g., ≥5% by weight Table 1 organic HAP, or crude/condensate)?
Do pumps, valves, or sampling connections operate in organic liquids service at least 300 hours per year?

candidates.title: Subpart MM

gates.question: Is the equipment a kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber?
gates.test: Yes -> Subpart MM monitoring/operating-limit rules apply; No -> Subpart MM does not apply
gates.quote: The owner or operator of each affected kraft or soda recovery furnace, kraft or soda lime kiln, sulfite combustion unit, or kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CPMS that can be used to determine and record the pressure drop across the scrubber

gates.question: Were the operating limits for the scrubber monitoring parameters established during an initial or periodic performance test (or based on previous performance tests)?
gates.test: Yes -> operating limits must be those test-derived values; No -> you must establish limits by conducting a performance test or use prior test data before changing limits
gates.quote: During the initial or periodic performance test required in § 63.865, the owner or operator of any affected source or process unit must establish operating limits for the monitoring parameters in paragraphs (e)(10) through (14) of this section

gates.question: Is the scrubber a smelt dissolving tank dynamic wet scrubber that operates at ambient pressure or a low-energy entrainment scrubber where fan speed does not vary so fan amperage or RPM may be used instead of pressure drop?
gates.test: Yes -> you may monitor fan amperage or RPM as an alternative to pressure drop (subject to the subpart's procedures); No -> pressure drop monitoring is required per CPMS rules
gates.quote: (iii) As an alternative to pressure drop measurement under paragraph (e)(10)(i) of this section, a monitoring device for measurement of fan amperage or fan revolutions per minute (RPM) may be used for smelt dissolving tank dynamic scrubbers

gates.question: Are you prepared to perform a subsequent performance test to expand or revise the operating limit (during which operating outside the prior limit to establish the new limit is allowed)?
gates.test: Yes -> you may establish expanded/replacement operating limits during a subsequent performance test and that test run does not count as an exceedance; No -> you cannot lawfully lower the operating limit without test-based establishment
gates.quote: Operating outside a previously established parameter limit during a performance test to expand the operating limit range does not constitute a monitoring exceedance.

missing: Whether the current 10 inches water column pressure-drop limit was originally established by an initial or subsequent performance test and the test data (three runs) used to set it
Whether you possess certified performance test data demonstrating compliance at a 5 inches water column pressure drop

Whether the smelt dissolving tank scrubber is a dynamic scrubber operating at ambient pressure or a low-energy entrainment scrubber with essentially constant fan speed (to allow fan-amperage or RPM monitoring)
Whether you plan to switch to monitoring fan amperage or RPM instead of pressure drop, and whether manufacturer-certified monitoring accuracy for amperage/RPM is available
Whether you will submit written notification to the Administrator and conduct a new/subsequent performance test to establish a revised operating limit

candidates.title: Subpart TTTTT

gates.question: Is the wet scrubber used to meet a particulate matter, PM10, chlorine, hydrochloric acid, or dioxins/furans emission limit subject to Subpart TTTTT Table 1?
gates.test: Yes -> Subpart TTTTT requires maintaining hourly average pressure drop and flow at or above the test-established minimum; No -> Subpart TTTTT likely does not apply
gates.quote: you must maintain the hourly average pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate at or above the minimum level established during the initial or subsequent performance test.

gates.question: Were site-specific operating limits (hourly average pressure drop and flow) established as the lowest average among compliant performance-test runs?
gates.test: Yes -> those test-derived lowest-average values are the required minimums; No -> you must perform a performance test to establish the operating limits before lowering them
gates.quote: Your operating limits are the lowest average individual pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate values in any of the three runs that meet the applicable emission limit.

gates.question: Will you submit written notification to the Administrator and conduct a new performance test to revise the operating limit to the proposed lower value?
gates.test: Yes -> follow the subpart's (f)(1)-(3) procedure to revise limits; No -> you may not lawfully lower the monitoring limit without conducting the required performance test and procedures
gates.quote: Submit a written notification to the Administrator of your request to conduct a new performance test to revise the operating limit.

missing: Whether this specific wet scrubber is being used to meet an emission limit listed in Table 1 to Subpart TTTTT
Whether initial or subsequent performance tests exist that establish the current (10 in. wc) limit and whether any test data support 5 in. wc
Whether you will submit the written notification and conduct a new performance test to demonstrate compliance at 5 in. wc

candidates.title: Subpart RRRRR

gates.question: Is the wet scrubber subject to performance testing in § 63.9620 and operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate in § 63.9590(b)(1)?
gates.test: Yes -> follow §63.9622 procedures to set site-specific operating limits from performance-test runs; No -> §63.9622 procedures do not apply
gates.quote: For wet scrubbers subject to performance testing in § 63.9620 and operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate in § 63.9590(b)(1), you must establish site-specific operating limits according to the procedures in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section.

gates.question: Were pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate measured (every 15 minutes) during each test run and averages calculated so the lowest average among runs established the operating limit?
gates.test: Yes -> the lowest average among the compliant runs becomes the operating limit; No -> a compliant performance test must be conducted to set or revise the limit
gates.quote: Your operating limits are established as the lowest average pressure drop and the lowest average scrubber water flow rate corresponding to any of the three test runs.

gates.question: Is the scrubber a rod-deck venturi scrubber applied to an indurating furnace so you may use historical certified performance-test pressure-drop data to establish a lower average pressure-drop limit?
gates.test: Yes -> you may use historical certified performance-test data (on/after Dec 18, 2002) to set a lower average pressure-drop limit (subject to conditions); No -> historical-data allowance does not apply
gates.quote: you may establish a lower average pressure drop operating limit by using historical average pressure drop data from a certified performance test completed on or after December 18, 2002

missing: Whether this scrubber is within the scope of § 63.9620/§ 63.9590(b)(1)
Whether you have three-run performance-test data establishing the current limit or historical certified performance-test data (post-Dec 18, 2002) applicable to the scrubber
Whether the scrubber is a rod-deck venturi on an indurating furnace (needed to use the historical-data allowance)

candidates.title: Subpart DDD

gates.question: Have you notified the Administrator of your desire to expand or change the control device/process operating parameter levels and obtained approval to conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new levels?
gates.test: Yes -> upon Administrator approval you must conduct additional performance tests and verify compliance before operating at new levels; No -> you must notify and obtain approval and tests before changing limits
gates.quote: Upon approval from the Administrator, you must conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new control device or process operating parameter levels.

missing: Whether Subpart DDD applies to this source (the quoted section is the subpart's procedural requirement)
Whether you have submitted a notification to the Administrator and received approval to change the monitored parameter limit
Whether you have scheduled or completed the required additional performance tests verifying compliance at the proposed lower limit

checklist.item: Confirm the scrubber is a kraft/soda smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber.
Provide the performance-test report(s) that established the current 10 in. wc pressure-drop operating limit (three-run averages and lowest-average derivation).

Confirm whether the scrubber is a dynamic smelt dissolving tank scrubber operating at ambient pressure or a low-energy entrainment scrubber with essentially constant fan speed (to consider fan-amperage/RPM monitoring).
If seeking a lower limit, confirm you will submit written notification to the Administrator and conduct a new or subsequent performance test to demonstrate compliance at the proposed 5 in. wc.
If claiming use of historical test data (for other subparts), provide certified historical performance-test data and applicability details (e.g., rod-deck venturi on indurating furnace).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants

gates.question: Do you operate a steel pickling facility or a hydrochloric acid regeneration plant that might be subject to Subpart CCC?
gates.test: yes -> consider Subpart CCC gates; no -> Subpart CCC likely not applicable
gates.quote: install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate. These flow rates must be monitored continuously

gates.question: Do you use a wet scrubber as the emission control device for the pickling line or acid regeneration plant?
gates.test: yes -> wet-scrubber monitoring and recording requirements apply under Subpart CCC; no -> other control-device monitoring rules apply
gates.quote: install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate. These flow rates must be monitored continuously

gates.question: While the scrubber is operating, do you monitor scrubber makeup and recirculation water flow rates continuously and record them at least once per shift?
gates.test: yes -> meets Subpart CCC's normal-recording-frequency requirement; no -> monitoring requirement violation unless alternative approved
gates.quote: install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate. These flow rates must be monitored continuously

gates.question: During performance tests used to establish operating parameters, do you monitor each operating parameter continuously and record with sufficient frequency, but no less frequently than once every 15 minutes?
gates.test: yes -> meets performance-test monitoring frequency requirement; no -> performance test monitoring requirement not met
gates.quote: During the emission test, each operating parameter must be monitored continuously and recorded with sufficient frequency to establish a representative average value for that parameter, but no less frequently than once every 15 minutes.

gates.question: Are you seeking Administrator approval for alternative monitoring requirements instead of those specified in Subpart CCC?
gates.test: yes -> you must obtain Administrator approval under the referenced provision; no -> standard Subpart CCC monitoring applies
gates.quote: The owner or operator may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements subject to approval by the Administrator.

gates.question: Is your facility an existing source required to have achieved initial compliance no later than June 22, 2001?
gates.test: yes -> compliance date already applied (June 22, 2001); no -> if new or reconstructed after Sept 18, 1997, different startup compliance timing applies
gates.quote: The owner or operator of an affected existing steel pickling facility and/or hydrochloric acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart shall achieve initial compliance with the requirements of this subpart no later than June 22, 2001.

missing: Whether each pickling line and the acid regeneration plant actually use wet scrubbers as their control devices
Whether each wet scrubber operates with recirculation (i.e., recirculation water flow rate applicability)
Definition of “shift” (length/timing) used for "recorded at least once per shift" in practice
Manufacturer certification and calibration schedule information for installed flow meters (certification to within 5 percent)

candidates.title: General Provisions (referenced)

gates.question: Do you intend to use any alternative combination of parameters to determine proportion of excess air that must be approved under subpart A §63.8(f)?
gates.test: yes -> you must obtain approval per §63.8(f) before using the alternative parameter set; no -> use the prescribed parameter combination
gates.quote: or by any other combination of parameters approved by the Administrator in accordance with § 63.8(f) of subpart A of this part.

missing: Full text of Subpart A (§§63.1–63.18) including §63.8(f) and §63.7 (procedures for performance testing and Administrator approval criteria) to determine approval process and alternatives

candidates.title: CPMS installation, operation, and maintenance requirements (Subpart TTTTT)

gates.question: Is your wet scrubber subject to the operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate in the referenced operating-limits section of Subpart TTTTT?
gates.test: yes -> CPMS installation/operation/maintenance requirements in Subpart TTTTT apply; no -> Subpart TTTTT CPMS requirements not applicable
gates.quote: For each wet scrubber subject to the operating limits in § 63.9890(b) for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate, you must install, operate, and maintain each CPMS according to the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section.

gates.question: Does your wet scrubber have a CPMS that completes at least one cycle every 15 minutes and provides valid data at least 95 percent of each averaging period?
gates.test: yes -> meets Subpart TTTTT CPMS cycle and data-validity expectations; no -> does not meet CPMS performance expectations
gates.quote: Each CPMS must complete a minimum of one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period. Each CPMS must have valid data for at least 95 percent of every averaging period. Each CPMS must determine and record the hourly average of all recorded readings.

gates.question: Does your CPMS determine and record the hourly average of all recorded readings?
gates.test: yes -> meets Subpart TTTTT requirement to compute and record hourly averages; no -> CPMS recording requirement not met
gates.quote: Each CPMS must determine and record the hourly average of all recorded readings.

missing: Whether the wet scrubber is subject to the specific operating-limits section (§63.9890(b)) referenced by Subpart TTTTT
Current CPMS configuration and whether it meets cycle, sensitivity, and data-validity criteria specified (sensor sensitivity, calibration frequency)

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements and CPMS provisions (Subpart EEEEE)

gates.question: Is your wet scrubber subject to the operating limits referenced in §63.7690(b)(2) such that Subpart EEEEE CPMS rules apply?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart EEEEE CPMS monitoring of 3-hour averages and recording applies; no -> these specific Subpart EEEEE provisions do not apply
gates.quote: For each wet scrubber subject to the operating limits in § 63.7690(b)(2), you must at all times monitor the 3-hour average pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate using CPMS according to the requirements in § 63.7741(c).

gates.question: Does your CPMS complete at least one 15-minute cycle and provide sufficient data to compute hourly and 3-hour averages as required by Subpart EEEEE?
gates.test: yes -> meets CPMS operational-frequency requirements; no -> CPMS operation not compliant with Subpart EEEEE expectations
gates.quote: Each CPMS must complete a minimum of one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period. You must have a minimum of three of the required four data points to constitute a valid hour of data. Each CPMS must determine and record the hourly average of all recorded readings and the 3-hour average of all recorded readings.

gates.question: For wet scrubbers subject to Subpart EEEEE, do you monitor and record the 3-hour average scrubber water (scrubbing liquid) flow rate using a CPMS?
gates.test: yes -> meets the specified 3-hour average monitoring requirement; no -> does not meet the Subpart EEEEE 3-hour monitoring requirement
gates.quote: For each wet scrubber subject to the operating limits in § 63.7690(b)(2), you must at all times monitor the 3-hour average pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate using CPMS according to the requirements in § 63.7741(c).

missing: Whether the scrubber is subject to the specific Subpart EEEEE operating-limits section (§63.7690(b)(2))
Details of CPMS (sensor sensitivity, calibration schedule) and whether the system computes/records hourly and 3-hour averages automatically

checklist.item: Confirm whether each pickling line and the acid regeneration plant use wet scrubbers as the control device (and which scrubbers have recirculation).
Verify whether each wet scrubber records makeup and recirculation water flow rates continuously and records them at least once per shift while operating.
Confirm whether performance-test monitoring captured operating parameters at least once every 15 minutes during runs used to set operating limits.
Determine whether the facility is an existing source subject to the Subpart CCC compliance date (initial compliance by June 22, 2001) or a new/reconstructed source.

If using alternative monitoring or alternative parameter combinations (e.g., to determine proportion of excess air), confirm whether Administrator approval under subpart A (§63.8(f)) has been obtained.
If CPMS are installed, verify they complete at least one cycle every 15 minutes and compute and record hourly (and, where required, 3-hour) averages and meet data-validity requirements.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous coating manufacturing

gates.question: Does your operation manufacture coatings as defined in § 63.8105?
gates.test: yes -> the operation falls within the industry category for this subpart; no -> this subpart's industry category likely does not apply
gates.quote: Coating means a material such as paint, ink, or adhesive that is intended to be applied to a substrate and consists of a mixture of resins, pigments, solvents, and/or other additives

gates.question: Is the portable mixer part of the miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations (process vessels, storage tanks, components, or wastewater tanks) at your facility?
gates.test: yes -> the mixer may be included in the affected source for this subpart; no -> the mixer may not be part of this affected source
gates.quote: Miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations include the facility-wide collection of equipment described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section that is used to manufacture coatings as defined in § 63.8105.

gates.question: Is your facility located at or part of a major source of HAP emissions as defined in section 112(a) of the CAA?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart's applicability requires being at or part of a major source; no -> this subpart does not apply based on the major source criterion
gates.quote: Are located at or are part of a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP) emissions, as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act (CAA);

gates.question: Does the vessel have a capacity greater than or equal to 250 gallons?
gates.test: yes -> the vessel meets the process vessel capacity threshold in the subpart definition; no -> the vessel does not meet the process vessel capacity threshold
gates.quote: portable tank or other vessel with a capacity greater than or equal to 250 gal and in which mixing, blending, diluting, dissolving, temporary holding, and other processing steps occur

gates.question: Is the operation exempt under the list of exclusions in § 63.7985(d) (e.g., research and development facilities or other listed exclusions)?
gates.test: yes -> the operation may be excluded from this subpart under the listed exemptions; no -> the exemptions do not apply
gates.quote: The requirements for miscellaneous coating manufacturing sources in this subpart do not apply to operations described in paragraphs (d)(1) through (5) of this section.

missing: Whether the facility is a major source (actual or potential annual HAP emissions)
Whether the 125-gallon portable mixer is used to manufacture coatings as defined in § 63.8105 (i.e., mixing/blending coating formulations)
Whether the mixer contains or contacts materials that are HAP (and HAP concentration)
Whether the mixer is assigned to another subpart's affected source at the facility (i.e., part of a separate regulated affected source)

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

gates.question: Does your facility perform surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts or products as described in § 63.3881(a)?
gates.test: yes -> the facility's activities are within the source category covered by this subpart; no -> this subpart's industry category likely does not apply
gates.quote: the source category to which this subpart applies is the surface coating of any miscellaneous metal parts and products, and it includes

gates.question: Is the portable mixer a mixing vessel in which coatings, thinners, or additives are stored or mixed and therefore part of the affected source's listed equipment?
gates.test: yes -> the mixer may be part of the affected source under this subpart; no -> the mixer may not be part of this affected source
gates.quote: The affected source is the collection of all of the items listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section that are used for surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products within each subcategory.

gates.question: Does the facility use 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products?
gates.test: yes -> the facility meets the usage threshold for applicability to this subpart (if also a major source or at/part of a major source); no -> the facility may be below this subpart's usage threshold
gates.quote: that uses 946 liters (250 gallons (gal)) per year, or more, of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products

gates.question: Are the coatings used in volumes less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and otherwise eligible for the small-volume exemption limits in § 63.3881(c)(3)?
gates.test: yes -> those small-volume coating uses can be exempted up to the facility limit; no -> the small-volume exemption does not apply
gates.quote: Coatings used in volumes of less than 189 liters (50 gal) per year, provided that the total volume of coatings exempt under this paragraph does not exceed 946 liters (250 gal) per year at the facility.

missing: Annual volume of HAP-containing coatings used at the facility (gallons/year)
Whether the 125-gallon portable mixer is used to mix/store coatings, thinners, or additives for surface coating operations
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP (actual or potential emissions)
Whether the mixer activity is part of surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts (vs. other activities)

gates.test: yes -> the facility activities fall within the industry category covered by this subpart; no -> this subpart's industry category likely does not apply
gates.quote: The affected source is the collection of all of the items listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section that are part of the large appliance surface coating facility:

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Site Remediation

gates.question: Do you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation?
gates.test: yes -> proceed to affected_source assessment; no -> this subpart does not apply to you
gates.quote: This subpart applies to you if you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation, as defined in § 63.7957;

gates.question: Does the remediation activity at your facility include process vents, remediation material management units, equipment components in remediation material service, or pressure relief devices?
gates.test: yes -> your site has affected sources regulated by this subpart; no -> no affected sources under this subpart
gates.quote: Process vents. The affected source is the entire group of process vents associated with the in-situ and ex-situ remediation processes used at your site to remove, destroy, degrade, transform, or immobilize hazardous substances

gates.question: Is your facility a major source of HAP (i.e., emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of a single HAP or ≥25 tons/year of combined HAP)?
gates.test: yes -> meets the major source condition for applicability; no -> does not meet the major source condition for applicability
gates.quote: A major source emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at the rate of 10 tons (9.07 megagrams) or more per year

gates.question: Is the total quantity of HAP in remediation material you remove during all site remediations at your facility less than 1 megagram (Mg) annually?
gates.test: yes -> you may be exempt from most requirements (recordkeeping still required); no -> the 1 Mg exemption does not apply
gates.quote: the remediation material excavated, extracted, pumped, or otherwise removed during all of the site remediations conducted at your facility is less than 1 megagram (Mg) annually

gates.question: Are the remediation activities at the site conducted by another entity (i.e., you do not conduct the remediation)?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart typically would not apply to you as the non-conducting owner/operator; no -> you conduct remediation and remain potentially subject to the subpart
gates.quote: This subpart applies to you if you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation, as defined in § 63.7957;

gates.question: Did construction or reconstruction of the affected remediation source commence before July 30, 2002?
gates.test: yes -> the affected source is considered existing; no -> the affected source may be considered new
gates.quote: Each affected source for your site is existing if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before July 30, 2002.

missing: Whether the current facility owner/operator (you) actually conducts the remediation activities or whether another party conducts them under a Consent Order
Whether the remediation material contains any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of subpart GGGGG
The facility-wide, annual total mass (megagrams or tons) of HAP contained in remediation materials removed (to evaluate the 1 Mg threshold)
Whether the remediation activities/units are co-located with one or more other stationary sources that meet an affected-source definition in other part 63 subparts
Dates when remediation construction or reconstruction commenced for the affected units (to determine new vs existing, including CERCLA/RCRA specific dates)

candidates.title: General Provisions (parts of §§ 63.1 through 63.15)

gates.question: Do the General Provisions in 40 CFR part 63 ( §§ 63.1 through 63.15) apply to your affected source(s) under this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> follow the applicable General Provisions identified for this subpart; no -> General Provisions do not apply
gates.quote: Table 3 of this subpart shows which parts of the General Provisions in §§ 63.1 through 63.15 apply to you.

missing: Which specific General Provisions (see Table 3 of subpart GGGGG) apply to your affected source(s) (Table 3 contents not provided in the supplied text)

checklist.item: Does your company currently perform (operate) the site remediation activities on the property, or did the previous owner retain operation under a Consent Order?
Do the remediation activities at the site involve process vents, remediation material management units, equipment components in remediation material service, or pressure relief devices?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy for any single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined)?
Is the total HAP mass in remediation material managed/removed from the facility less than 1 megagram (1 Mg) per year (facility-wide)?

candidates.title: Hazardous waste combustors (Subpart EEE)

gates.question: Is your unit a hazardous waste combustor (e.g., a hazardous waste incinerator)?
gates.test: yes -> This subpart (EEE) applies; no -> This subpart does not apply
gates.quote: The provisions of this subpart apply to all hazardous waste combustors: hazardous waste incinerators, hazardous waste cement kilns, hazardous waste lightweight aggregate kilns, hazardous waste solid fuel boilers, hazardous waste liquid fuel boilers, and hazardous waste hydrochloric acid production furnaces.

gates.question: Do you have multiple distinct combustion chambers (e.g., a rotary kiln plus a secondary combustion chamber) where controlled flame combustion of hazardous waste occurs?
gates.test: yes -> Each combustion chamber is measured/treated individually (establish limits per chamber); no -> May be considered a single combustion chamber for operating parameter purposes
gates.quote: Combustion chamber means the area in which controlled flame combustion of hazardous waste occurs. Continuous monitor means a device which continuously samples the regulated parameter specified in § 63.1209 without interruption,

gates.question: Is your facility a major source of hazardous air pollutants (i.e., subject to Title V permitting obligations)?
gates.test: yes -> Major source obligations (e.g., Title V) apply and should be accounted for; no -> Area source status applies (different permitting considerations)
gates.quote: Major sources subject to this subpart, but not previously subject to title V, are immediately subject to the requirement to apply for and obtain a title V permit in all states,

gates.question: Have you applied to the Administrator to waive the minimum combustion chamber temperature (i.e., submitted an application to waive an operating parameter limit)?
gates.test: yes -> If approved by the Administrator the minimum temperature limit may be waived; no -> The minimum combustion chamber temperature operating parameter limit applies
gates.quote: You may submit an application to waive an operating parameter limit specified in this section based on documentation that neither that operating parameter limit nor an alternative operating parameter limit is needed to ensure compliance.

gates.question: Did you submit any waiver/alternative monitoring application to the Administrator at the time you submitted your comprehensive performance test plan (i.e., not later than with the test plan)?
gates.test: yes -> Application timing requirement met (will be reviewed with the test plan); no -> Application may be untimely (must be submitted with test plan per procedures)
gates.quote: Timing of the application. You must submit the application to the Administrator not later than with the comprehensive performance test plan. Content of the application. You must include in the application:

Title V / major-source status of the facility (to determine permitting and procedural obligations).

Document whether each unit (rotary kiln and secondary combustion chamber) meets the definition of a combustion chamber (area of controlled flame combustion) and whether they are distinct chambers.

Verify whether an application to waive the minimum combustion chamber temperature operating parameter limit has been prepared and submitted to the Administrator with the comprehensive performance test plan.
Confirm whether the facility is a Title V major source (subject to Title V permitting) or an area source.
Identify and document proposed temperature measurement locations for each combustion chamber in the performance test plan.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Metal Furniture

gates.question: Do you perform surface coating of metal furniture (coating applied to a substrate and the product is furniture or components constructed entirely or partially from metal)?
gates.test: yes -> source is in the metal furniture surface coating category; no -> this subpart's source category likely does not apply
gates.quote: Surface coating is the application of coatings to a substrate using, for example, spray guns or dip tanks. Metal furniture means furniture or components of furniture constructed either entirely or partially from metal.

gates.question: Do you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source as defined in § 63.4882?

gates.quote: that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (Mg) (10 tons) or more per year

gates.quote: Surface coating conducted at an affected source that uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP.

gates.question: Is the surface coating of metal components conducted in an operation that is subject to the wood furniture manufacturing NESHAP in subpart JJ?

gates.quote: Surface coating of metal components of wood furniture conducted in an operation that is subject to the wood furniture manufacturing NESHAP in subpart JJ of this part.

gates.test: yes -> (n/a) determine the compliance start date from §63.4883 to compute initial compliance period; no -> (n/a) you still must identify the applicable compliance date

gates.question: Was the previous transfer efficiency test conducted using the methods specified in this subpart (e.g., ASTM D5066-91 or the EPA primer/topcoat protocol)?

gates.test: Yes -> Previous test may only be used if you can demonstrate the results remain reliable despite changes; No -> This condition supports using the previous test (subject to approval).

gates.question: For VOC/HAP gas-phase analysis, are the target concentrations for each HAP between 150 parts per billion by volume and 100 parts per million by volume so that ASTM D6420-18 may be used?
gates.test: yes -> ASTM D6420-18 may be used under the rule's conditions; no -> ASTM D6420-18 is not allowed and another validated method is needed
gates.quote: You may use ASTM D6420-18 (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14), to determine compliance ... if the target concentration for each HAP is between 150 parts per billion by volume and 100 ppmv.

Representative sampling plan and number of samples for liquids (Method 311/ASTM D6886 guidance)

checklist.item: Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant (NGL extraction or fractionation) or processes/upgrades/stores hydrocarbon liquids prior to custody transfer.
Identify the specific ancillary equipment and compressors and whether each contacts field gas prior to NGL extraction (wet gas) or contacts processed streams.
Obtain representative composition data (gas and liquid) for each stream to be assessed, sufficient to calculate total VHAP weight-percent.
Determine whether each piece of equipment operates in VHAP service ≥300 hours/year (for §63.769 applicability).
Verify whether target HAP concentrations for gas-phase analysis fall between 150 ppbv and 100 ppmv (to permit ASTM D6420 use per EEEE).
Decide which analytical method you will use (Method 18, ASTM D6420, Method 311, or ASTM D6886) and prepare sampling plan consistent with that method.

candidates.title: General Provisions

gates.question: Do you intend to assert a claim of force majeure that delayed testing beyond the performance test deadline?
gates.test: yes -> You must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and follow §63.7(a)(4) procedures; no -> Normal performance test deadlines and requirements apply.
gates.quote: The owner or operator shall notify the Administrator, in writing as soon as practicable following the date the owner or operator first knew

gates.question: Was the performance test completed within 180 days of the compliance date for the affected source?
gates.test: yes -> Deadline met; no -> The owner/operator is subject to deadlines unless a force majeure extension or waiver is approved.
gates.quote: the owner or operator of the affected source must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date for such source.

missing: Date of the affected source's compliance date
Whether a written force majeure notification has been sent to the Administrator and on what date
Details of the proposed replacement performance test date and measures to minimize delay

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Iron and Steel Foundries

gates.question: Is your facility an iron and steel foundry subject to Subpart EEEEE?
gates.test: yes -> Continue evaluating Subpart EEEEE applicability and deadlines; no -> Subpart EEEEE does not apply.
gates.quote: you must conduct a performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date that is specified in § 63.7683 for your iron and steel foundry

gates.question: Do the emissions limitations in § 63.7690 apply to the processes (including Phase 1 melting) at your foundry?
gates.test: yes -> Those applicable emissions limitations require initial compliance demonstrations (performance tests or other) per §63.7730; no -> That particular §63.7690 limit does not drive the initial test requirement for that process.
gates.quote: for your iron and steel foundry to demonstrate initial compliance with each emissions limitation in § 63.7690 that applies to you.

gates.question: Has 180 calendar days elapsed since the compliance date specified in § 63.7683 for your foundry without completing the required performance test?
gates.test: yes -> You are past the default initial performance test deadline (subject to §63.7(a)(4) force majeure procedures); no -> You remain within the 180-day window.

Which specific emissions limitations in § 63.7690 apply to each process/furnace

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Metal Parts and Products (metal melting furnace testing provisions)

gates.test: yes -> Subpart ZZZZZ initial performance testing requirements likely apply to those furnaces/buildings; no -> Subpart ZZZZZ initial testing requirements for metal melting furnaces do not apply.
gates.quote: for each metal melting furnace or group of all metal melting furnaces that is subject to an emissions limit in § 63.10895(c) and for each building

gates.question: Was the initial performance test for applicable metal melting furnace(s) conducted within 180 days of your compliance date and reported in your notification of compliance status?
gates.test: yes -> Initial test deadline met and results should have been reported; no -> You missed the 180-day default deadline unless an extension or force majeure claim under §63.7(a)(4) or the subpart's reporting-force majeure provisions applies.
gates.quote: You must conduct the test within 180 days of your compliance date and report the results in your notification of compliance status.

missing: Which specific metal melting furnaces are subject to § 63.10895(c) at the facility
The facility's compliance date for Subpart ZZZZZ
Whether there is a qualifying prior performance test within the last 5 years that you intend to use
Whether you have notified the Administrator of any delay or submitted a force majeure claim

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Integrated Iron and Steel (notifications, reporting, force majeure for electronic submissions)

gates.question: Have you submitted performance test results required by this subpart within 60 calendar days after completing each performance test?
gates.test: yes -> Results were timely submitted; no -> You missed the 60-day results submittal requirement and may seek relief only as allowed (e.g., claim of force majeure per this subpart).
gates.quote: Within 60 calendar days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test

gates.question: Do you intend to assert a claim of force majeure to excuse or extend an electronic reporting/submittal deadline (CEDRI/CDX) for performance test results or reports?
gates.test: yes -> You must notify the Administrator in writing promptly and provide the written description and rationale per §63.7841(f); no -> Normal electronic submittal deadlines apply.
gates.quote: For the purposes of this section, a force majeure event is defined as an event that will be or has been caused by circumstances beyond the control of the affected facility, its contractors, or any entity controlled by the affected facility

missing: Whether your required submittals (performance test results or reports) must be made electronically via CEDRI/CDX

Whether a written force majeure notification has been sent to the Administrator and its contents

Confirm which metal melting furnaces at the facility are subject to § 63.10895(c) (Subpart ZZZZZ applicability).
Determine the compliance date applicable to your affected source and whether the 180-day performance test deadline has passed.
Verify whether a written notification to the Administrator asserting force majeure (per §63.7(a)(4) or subpart-specific procedures) has been submitted and the date of that notification.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Cellulose Products Manufacturing (Subpart UUUU)

gates.question: Does your facility operate a cellulose food casing (viscose) process unit?
gates.test: yes => Subpart UUUU is a candidate; no => Subpart UUUU is not a candidate
gates.quote: Cellulose food casing means a cellulose casing, which is manufactured using the viscose process, used in forming meat products (e.g., hot dogs, sausages) and, in most cases, removed from the meat products before sale.

gates.question: Will the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 be used as a continuous emissions/parameter monitoring system (CEMS/CPMS) to measure hydrogen sulfide or organic HAPs for compliance under this subpart?
gates.test: yes => must meet PS-7/PS-9 or request alternative monitoring approval under Subpart A; no => different monitoring provisions may apply
gates.quote: (i) PS-7 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B, for CEMS used to measure hydrogen sulfide emissions; (iii) PS-9 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B, for CEMS that use gas chromatography to measure organic HAP emissions;

gates.question: Do you have a site-specific monitoring plan and has the CMS been performance-evaluated and installed per the subpart's OM&M requirements?
gates.test: yes => proceed with operation per plan; no => must prepare/complete site-specific monitoring plan and performance evaluation per subpart before relying on CMS data

Whether the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 will be used as a CMS/CEMS/CPMS for regulatory compliance or for non-regulatory/operational monitoring
Whether the instrument will be installed at a compliance-critical location (e.g., control device outlet) or elsewhere
Whether a site-specific monitoring plan or prior Administrator approvals already exist for this instrument

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

gates.test: yes => §63.8 procedures for CMS and alternatives apply; no => §63.8 CMS-specific provisions may not apply

gates.question: Do you plan to use the new instrument as an alternative to a monitoring method or procedure specified in the relevant standard?
gates.test: yes => you must apply to the Administrator for approval under §63.8(f); no => follow the monitoring method specified in the relevant standard
gates.quote: After receipt and consideration of written application, the Administrator may approve alternatives to any monitoring methods or procedures of this part including, but not limited to, the following:

gates.quote: If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method that is to be used to demonstrate compliance with a relevant standard, the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin and must meet the requirements for an alternative test method under § 63.7(f).

missing: Whether the new instrument will be used as the performance evaluation/test method
Whether an application for an alternative monitoring method has already been submitted or approved
Whether you intend to seek a minor change (site-specific) versus intermediate/major change approval

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks (Subpart H)

gates.question: Is the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 being used to perform Method 21 leak screening or to replace a Method 21/GC/PID portable analyzer for equipment leak monitoring?
gates.test: yes => Method 21 performance criteria, response factor adjustments, and calibration requirements apply; no => Method 21 provisions may not be applicable
gates.quote: Except as provided for in paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section, the detection instrument shall meet the performance criteria of Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, except the instrument response factor criteria in Section 3.1.2(a) of Method 21 shall be for the average composition of the process fluid not each individual VOC in the stream.

gates.question: Will the instrument be calibrated daily and with the calibration gases and procedures specified for Method 21 if used for leak detection per this subpart?
gates.test: yes => follow Method 21 daily calibration procedures and specified calibration gases; no => you may need to justify alternative calibration or seek approval
gates.quote: The instrument shall be calibrated before use on each day of its use by the procedures specified in Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A.

missing: Whether the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 meets Method 21 performance criteria or will be adjusted by response factors
Which calibration gases and concentrations you will use for daily calibrations and audits if performing Method 21 screening
Whether the replacement instrument will be used for equipment leak detection subject to Subpart H leak definitions

gates.question: Are you considering replacing parametric monitoring with a CEMS to measure control device outlet total organic or HAP emissions concentration?

gates.quote: As an alternative to the parametric monitoring required in this subpart, you may install, calibrate, and operate a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) to measure the control device outlet total organic emissions or organic HAP emissions concentration.

gates.test: yes => you must conduct the performance evaluation per §63.8 and the cited Performance Specifications; no => you cannot rely on CEMS alternative without required performance evaluation
gates.quote: You must conduct a performance evaluation of the CEMS according to the requirements in § 63.8 and Performance Specification 8 (for a total organic emissions CEMS) or Performance Specification 9 (for a HAP emissions CEMS).

missing: Whether the control device and monitoring in your process fall under the parametric-monitoring provisions of subpart GGGGG (i.e., whether this 'alternative to parametric monitoring' path is available to you)
Whether the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 can meet the applicable performance specifications (or whether you will request an alternative)

checklist.item: Confirm whether the facility operates cellulose food casing viscose process units (i.e., is a cellulose food casing operation).
Confirm whether the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 will be used as a compliance CEMS/CPMS (control device outlet or other compliance point) measuring H2S or carbon disulfide (organic HAP).
Confirm whether you plan to use the new instrument as the performance-test/performance-evaluation method (if so, prepare alternative-monitoring application at least 60 days before evaluation).
Confirm whether the Model 8900 will be used for Method 21 equipment leak screening (and whether it meets Method 21 performance/calibration criteria or requires response-factor adjustment).

candidates.title: General Provisions

gates.question: Is the affected source meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis, or operating under an extension of compliance or a requested extension still under consideration?
gates.test: yes -> Administrator may consider waiving an individual performance test for continuous compliance or extension; no -> cannot rely on continuous-compliance/extension ground for a waiver

candidates.title: Surface Coating Operations (performance testing procedures)

gates.question: Are the argon stir station exhausts and the baghouse inlet vented to the same common control device (i.e., do multiple emission points share the same baghouse)?
gates.test: yes -> only one performance test may be required for that group of emission points; no -> separate performance tests may be required unless other provisions apply
gates.quote: If multiple emission points are vented to one common control device to meet the requirements of § 63.703 (c), (d)(2), (e)(1), and (f)(1), only one performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance for that group of emission points

gates.question: During a performance test, can the affected emission points be isolated from other gaseous emission sources (for example by a temporary total enclosure or by shutting down other non-affected sources) to enable testing?
gates.test: yes -> owner/operator may isolate affected points and proceed with a performance test for those points; no -> must consider other demonstration approaches or request alternative methods/waiver
gates.quote: During a performance test, the owner or operator of affected HAP emission points located in an area with other gaseous emission sources not affected by this subpart shall isolate the affected HAP emission points from all other gaseous emission points by one of the following methods:

missing: Whether the argon stir station emission points are classified under the source category covered by subpart EE (for applicability) and whether the baghouse and emissions are configured as 'multiple emission points vented to one common control device' per the regulation

candidates.title: Extension, waivers, and alternatives (Subpart YY)

gates.question: Can you demonstrate continuous compliance, or are you operating under an extension (or have requested an extension that is still under consideration), as a basis for requesting a waiver of a performance test?
gates.test: yes -> you may apply for a waiver of an individual performance test under the subpart's waiver provisions; no -> this waiver ground is not available
gates.quote: Individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis

gates.question: Can you document and include in a waiver application technical, economic, or impracticality justifications explaining why the affected source cannot perform the required performance test?
gates.test: yes -> application should include this information and may be considered; no -> application would lack required justification information
gates.quote: Any application for a waiver of a performance test shall include information justifying the owner or operator's request for a waiver, such as the technical or economic infeasibility, or the impracticality, of the affected source performing the required test.

missing: Whether an application for a waiver or extension has already been submitted and what supporting justification (technical, economic, or impracticality) the facility can provide

candidates.title: Electric Arc Furnaces and AOD Vessels (EAF/AOD)

gates.question: Are the argon stir station emissions combined in the baghouse with emissions from other sources not subject to the same subpart (for example, a ladle metallurgical furnace or other non-subpart sources)?
gates.test: yes -> you must notify and receive Administrator approval for procedures to determine compliance when emissions are combined with sources not subject to this subpart; no -> standard performance-testing procedures apply
gates.quote: You must notify and receive approval from the Administrator for procedures that will be used to determine compliance for an EAF or AOD vessel when emissions are combined with those from facilities not subject to this subpart.

gates.question: Was a previous performance test conducted for the same emissions source within the past 5 years using the specified methods and representative conditions, so you could certify initial compliance based on that prior test?
gates.test: yes -> prior test results may be used in lieu of a new initial performance test if they meet the subpart's conditions; no -> an initial performance test is required unless another waiver/alternative is approved
gates.quote: you may certify initial compliance with the applicable emission limit for one or more emissions sources based on the results of a previous performance test for that emissions source in lieu of the requirement for an initial performance test

missing: Whether the facility operates EAF/AOD vessels or whether the argon stir stations are covered by this subpart; whether prior performance tests exist for the same emission points and whether those tests meet the 'representative' and method requirements

checklist.item: Determine whether the argon stir station vents and the ladle metallurgical furnace vents are ducted to the same baghouse (i.e., a single common control device).
If ducts are shared, determine whether prior performance testing was conducted for these emission points within the last 5 years using the specified methods and representative conditions.
Document whether the source has been meeting the relevant emission standard(s) on a continuous basis, or whether an extension/request for extension has been granted or is pending.

Prepare technical justification showing why separate performance testing of the argon stir stations is impractical (e.g., inability to isolate emissions, influence from other controlled sources), to include with any waiver application.
If emissions are combined with sources not in the same subpart, confirm whether you have notified and received approval from the Administrator for alternate compliance/test procedures.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Hydrochloric Acid Production

gates.question: Does your facility produce liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations?
gates.test: yes: facility may be subject to Subpart NNNNN; no: this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during its normal operations

gates.question: Does the Irgafos V-47 scrubber mix an aqueous caustic stream with exhaust gases from an HCl process vent, storage tank, or transfer operation to control HCl and/or Cl2?
gates.test: yes: the device is a caustic scrubber control device under this subpart; no: this caustic-scrubber control-device definition may not apply
gates.quote: mixes an aqueous stream or slurry containing a caustic substance with the exhaust gases from an HCl process vent, HCl storage tank, or HCl transfer operation

gates.question: Is the HCl production facility located at, or part of, a major source of HAP?
gates.test: yes: the facility meets the major-source criterion for Subpart NNNNN applicability; no: Subpart NNNNN may not apply as written to an area source
gates.quote: A major source of HAP emissions is any stationary source or group of stationary sources within a contiguous area under common control that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year

gates.question: Have you (or will you) conduct a performance test that measured scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate so a minimum value can be established as the operating limit?
gates.test: yes: the scrubber flow minimum must be based on performance test values per the subpart; no: you cannot establish the minimum as required without such test data
gates.quote: The minimum value shall be based on the scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate, as appropriate, values measured during the performance test.

gates.question: Is the facility excluded because it is part of a chlor-alkali facility producing HCl by direct synthesis of hydrogen and chlorine?
gates.test: yes: Subpart NNNNN does not apply per this exemption; no: exemption does not apply
gates.quote: An HCl production facility is not subject to this subpart if it produces HCl through the direct synthesis of hydrogen and chlorine and is part of a chlor-alkali facility.

gates.question: Have you conducted performance testing under conditions representative of normal operations as required for establishing operating limits?
gates.test: yes: operating limits based on the test support monitoring and compliance per the subpart; no: you must conduct representative performance testing before establishing compliant operating limits
gates.quote: you must conduct each performance test under conditions representative of normal operations. The owner or operator must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test

missing: Whether the liquid HCl product concentration is >= 30 weight percent at this facility
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP (tons/year or potential to emit)
Whether the Irgafos V-47 scrubber is configured/used to control HCl/Cl2 process vent, storage tank, or transfer emissions
Whether a representative performance test has been conducted and what scrubber flow, recirculation, and effluent pH values were measured
Whether the facility proposes to submit an alternative monitoring plan per §63.8(f) or a design evaluation in lieu of performance testing

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling—HCl Process Facilities and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants

gates.question: Is the facility subject to 40 CFR part 63 Subpart CCC (steel pickling/HCl regeneration) instead of Subpart NNNNN?
gates.test: yes: Subpart CCC governs and Subpart NNNNN would not apply; no: Subpart CCC does not apply and Subpart NNNNN may apply
gates.quote: 40 CFR part 63, subpart CCC, National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling—HCl Process Facilities and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants.

gates.question: Do you use a wet scrubber to achieve compliance such that the performance test must establish minimum makeup and minimum recirculation water flow rates?
gates.test: yes: Subpart CCC requires establishing site-specific minimum makeup and recirculation flow rates during performance testing; no: this specific CCC requirement may not apply
gates.quote: During the performance test for each emission control device, the owner or operator using a wet scrubber to achieve compliance shall establish site-specific operating parameter values for the minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and, for scrubbers that operate with recirculation, the minimum recirculation water flow rate.

gates.question: Will you conduct multiple performance tests if you seek to establish alternative compliant operating parameter values?
gates.test: yes: Subpart CCC explicitly allows multiple performance tests to establish alternative compliant operating parameter values; no: you must rely on the existing established parameter values from initial testing
gates.quote: An owner or operator may conduct multiple performance tests to establish alternative compliant operating parameter values.

missing: Whether the facility is in the source category covered by Subpart CCC (steel pickling or HCl regeneration) rather than an HCl production facility covered by NNNNN
Whether the wet caustic scrubber is used to achieve compliance under Subpart CCC and existing performance test data for makeup and recirculation flow
Performance test records showing the flow rates and any site-specific operating parameter values already established

candidates.title: Procedures for approval of alternative means of emission limitation

gates.question: Are you requesting approval to use an alternative means of emission limitation (an alternative to design, equipment, work practice, or operational standards) under the alternative-means procedure?
gates.test: yes: you may request an alternative-means determination under this procedure; no: this specific alternative-means approval process does not apply
gates.quote: An owner or operator of an affected source may request a determination of alternative means of emission limitation to the requirements of design, equipment, work practice, or operational standards of this subpart or of a subpart referenced by this subpart.

gates.question: Can you collect, verify, and submit information showing the alternative means (including proposed monitoring) achieves emission reductions at least equivalent to the standard?
gates.test: yes: submit the information and proposed test plan to seek approval; no: you have not provided the required equivalence demonstration
gates.quote: In order to obtain approval, any person seeking permission to use an alternative means of compliance under this section shall collect, verify, and submit to the Administrator information showing that the alternative means achieves equivalent emission reductions.

missing: Test data, engineering analyses, or proposed test plan demonstrating that 65 gpm recirculation and >=2% caustic concentration achieve equivalent HCl/Cl2 control compared to established standards
A description of proposed monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting to demonstrate ongoing equivalence as required by the submittal provisions

candidates.title: General Provisions (compliance, alternative standards, and procedures)

gates.question: Do you intend to rely on approval of an alternative nonopacity emission standard or alternative means under the general §63.6 provisions (e.g., §63.6(g))?
gates.test: yes: §63.6(g) provides a route for Administrator to permit alternative nonopacity emission standards after public notice; no: general §63.6 alternative-standard process is not being invoked
gates.quote: the Administrator will publish in the Federal Register a notice permitting the use of the alternative emission standard for purposes of compliance with the promulgated standard.

gates.question: Can you submit the proposed test plan or results and procedures in accordance with §§63.7 and 63.8 as required when requesting permission to use an alternative standard under §63.6(g)?
gates.test: yes: you must submit a proposed test plan or test results per the cited provisions; no: you have not prepared the required submission
gates.quote: submit a proposed test plan or the results of testing and monitoring in accordance with § 63.7 and § 63.8,

missing: Whether you will submit a §63.6(g) request and the planned contents (test plan, monitoring/QA/QC, equivalence demonstration)
Whether any state or EPA authority has been contacted regarding submission and public-notice process

checklist.item: Confirm the liquid HCl product concentration produced during normal operations (weight percent).
Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAP (actual or potential to emit ≥10 tons single HAP or ≥25 tons total HAP).
Confirm that the Irgafos V-47 scrubber is used to control HCl and/or Cl2 emissions from HCl process vents, storage tanks, or transfer operations.
Provide results (or schedule) of representative performance testing that measured scrubber inlet/recirculation flow and effluent pH.
Provide engineering analysis or test data showing that 65 gpm recirculation and ≥2% caustic achieve equivalent HCl/Cl2 control (for an alternative-means submittal).
Confirm whether the facility is covered by Subpart CCC (steel pickling/HCl regeneration) instead of Subpart NNNNN.
