candidates.title: Bulk Gasoline Terminals (continuous monitoring)

gates.question: Is your facility a bulk gasoline terminal that is subject to the provisions referenced in §63.422(b)(1) or §63.422(b)(2)?
gates.test: yes -> this subpart's monitoring rules are potentially applicable; no -> this subpart is not applicable
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) shall install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain, according to the manufacturer's specifications, a continuous monitoring system (CMS)

gates.question: Does your vapor control use a thermal oxidation system (combustion device) or a flare or other vapor processing system listed in §63.427(a)(1)–(4)?
gates.test: yes -> specific monitoring parameter (temperature or pilot-flame) in §63.427(a)(1)–(4) applies; no -> §63.427 monitoring provisions for those devices do not apply
gates.quote: Where a thermal oxidation system is used, a CPMS capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

gates.question: Do you intend to propose monitoring an alternative operating parameter (not the listed temperature/TOC/pressure parameters) and demonstrate to the Administrator that it shows continuous compliance?
gates.test: yes -> you must demonstrate to the Administrator's satisfaction per §63.427(a)(5); no -> you must monitor the listed parameter(s)
gates.quote: Monitoring an alternative operating parameter or a parameter of a vapor processing system other than those listed in this paragraph will be allowed upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard

missing: Whether this specific terminal is subject to §63.422(b)(1) or §63.422(b)(2) (which determines which CMS provisions apply)
Which vapor control device your terminal uses for gasoline loading (thermal oxidation, flare, carbon adsorption, refrigerated condenser, etc.)
Whether Administrator approval for an alternative parameter has been sought or is planned

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Bulk Gasoline Terminals (Modernized requirements)

gates.question: Is your facility a bulk gasoline terminal that is subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to this subpart (i.e., this subpart applies to your terminal)?
gates.test: yes -> the monitoring and testing requirements in §63.11092 apply; no -> this subpart's requirements do not apply
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to this subpart must comply with the requirements in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.

gates.question: Does your vapor processing/control system for loading racks use a thermal oxidation system (or a flare) that would trigger the thermal oxidation/flare monitoring paragraphs in §63.11092(b)(1)(iii) or (b)(2)/(b)(3)?
gates.test: yes -> the specific monitoring options (temperature CPMS or pilot-flame sensor) in §63.11092(b)(1)(iii) apply; no -> those specific thermal-oxidation/flare monitoring options do not apply
gates.quote: The presence of a thermal oxidation system pilot flame shall be monitored using a heat-sensing device, such as an ultraviolet beam sensor or a thermocouple, installed in proximity of the pilot light, to indicate the presence of a flame.

gates.question: Do you intend to use the pilot-flame presence (heat-sensing device) as the approved monitoring parameter instead of combustion-zone temperature (i.e., rely on the alternative monitoring provisions in §63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B))?
gates.test: yes -> you must meet the alternative-plan/inspection/automatic-prevent-loading requirements specified in §63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B)(1)–(2); no -> you must use the CPMS temperature monitoring described in §63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(A)
gates.quote: The thermal oxidation system shall be equipped to automatically prevent gasoline loading operations from beginning at any time that the pilot flame is absent.

gates.question: Has the required continuous monitoring system (CMS) been installed by the subpart's applicable deadline (e.g., for many facilities, CMS must be installed by January 10, 2011)?
gates.test: yes -> you meet the installation deadline; no -> confirm current compliance schedule or request relief/alternatives
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the provisions of this subpart shall install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain, according to the manufacturer's specifications, a continuous monitoring system (CMS) while gasoline vapors are displaced to the vapor processor systems

missing: Whether this terminal is subject to the specific Table 2 item(s) referenced (item 1(b) or other items)
Which specific control device is used on the loading rack (thermal oxidizer vs flare vs other)
Whether the facility has or will submit the monitoring and inspection plan and seek Administrator approval where required

candidates.title: General Control Device and Work Practice Requirements (flares and alternative work practice)

gates.question: Is the control device you plan to monitor a flare that is used to comply with applicable subpart requirements?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart A flare monitoring provisions (presence of pilot flame) apply to flares used for compliance; no -> Subpart A flare-specific provisions do not apply
gates.quote: Flares shall be operated at all times when emissions may be vented to them. Flares shall be operated with a flame present at all times. The presence of a flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device

gates.question: Do you intend to monitor the presence of a pilot flame (thermocouple or equivalent) rather than monitoring combustion-zone temperature?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart A requires pilot-flame presence monitoring for flares and permits thermocouples/equivalents; no -> other monitoring specified by the applicable subpart remains required
gates.quote: The presence of a flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device to detect the presence of a flame.

gates.question: Are you seeking to use an alternative work practice (not Method 21) for leak detection or an alternative parameter that would rely on Subpart A procedures?
gates.test: yes -> you must follow Subpart A alternative work practice provisions and recordkeeping/reporting; no -> Subpart A alternative work practice provisions are not used
gates.quote: This section contains requirements for control devices used to comply with applicable subparts of this part. The requirements are placed here for administrative convenience and apply only to facilities covered by subparts referring to this section.

missing: Whether the specific control device is a flare and is being used to comply with an applicable subpart requirement
Whether any subpart-specific monitoring (e.g., temperature CPMS) is mandatory instead of pilot-flame monitoring for the particular applicability

candidates.title: Process Vent Provisions—monitoring requirements (incinerators/flares/boilers/scrubbers)

gates.question: Does your operation include a process vent that uses a combustion device (incinerator, flare, boiler/process heater) to comply with applicable process-vent standards?
gates.test: yes -> §63.114 monitoring provisions for combustion devices may apply; no -> §63.114 does not apply
gates.quote: Each owner or operator of a process vent that uses a combustion device to comply with the requirements in § 63.113(a)(1), (2), or (5) ... shall install monitoring equipment specified in paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6)

gates.question: If you use an incinerator or boiler/process heater, is the specified monitoring a temperature device in the firebox (for incinerators/boilers) or a pilot-flame detector for flares?
gates.test: yes -> follow the specific device-monitoring choices in §63.114(a)(1) and (2); no -> seek alternative monitoring approval per §63.114(c)
gates.quote: Where an incinerator other than a catalytic incinerator is used, a temperature monitoring device shall be installed in the firebox ... Where a flare is used, except as specified in § 63.108(a), the following monitoring equipment is required: A device ... capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame.

gates.question: Do you plan to request approval to monitor a parameter other than those listed for the combustion device (i.e., submit an alternative monitoring request under §63.114(c))?
gates.test: yes -> submit request per §63.114(c) to the Administrator; no -> monitor the parameters listed in §63.114(a)/(b)
gates.quote: An owner or operator of a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent may request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) of this section. The request shall be submitted according to the procedures specified in § 63.655(h).

missing: Whether your gasoline terminal's vapor control functions are regulated as a process vent under Subpart G (i.e., whether §63.113 applies)
Device type (incinerator vs flare vs boiler) for the specific vent(s) at issue
Whether you will submit an alternative monitoring approval request and the technical rationale

checklist.item: Confirm the facility is a bulk gasoline terminal and determine which subpart/table item (e.g., Table 2 item 1(b)) designates applicability.
Identify the vapor control device used on the loading rack(s): thermal oxidizer (incinerator), flare, carbon adsorber, refrigerated condenser, or other.
If using a thermal oxidizer, confirm whether you currently measure combustion-zone/firebox temperature (CPMS) and whether you seek to substitute pilot-flame presence monitoring.
If proposing pilot-flame monitoring as an alternative parameter, prepare/confirm a monitoring and inspection plan and whether Administrator approval is required or already obtained.
Confirm whether the facility has met the subpart-specific CMS installation/compliance dates (e.g., CMS installed by Jan 10, 2011 where applicable).

candidates.title: Subpart CCC

gates.question: Is your facility a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC?
gates.test: yes -> consider Subpart CCC gates; no -> Subpart CCC not applicable
gates.quote: (a) The owner or operator of a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart shall: (1) Conduct performance tests to measure the HCl mass flows at the control device inlet and outlet

gates.question: Do you use a wet scrubber (e.g., an HCl bubbler) as the emission control device for HCl emissions?
gates.test: yes -> monitoring requirements for wet scrubbers apply; no -> other control-device monitoring rules apply
gates.quote: if a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device, install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate

gates.question: Can you obtain Administrator approval to develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements?
gates.test: yes -> alternative monitoring may be implemented after approval; no -> must follow default monitoring requirements in this subpart
gates.quote: calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions but not less frequently than once per year. The owner or operator may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements subject to approval by the Administrator.

missing: Whether this facility is actually a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant covered by Subpart CCC
Whether the HCl bubbler is considered a wet scrubber under the subpart
Results/values from the performance test that would establish baseline operating limits (e.g., makeup flow, recirculation flow, immersion depth)
Whether an alternative monitoring plan has been or will be submitted to the Administrator under §63.8(f)

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN

gates.question: Will you request approval to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubber control devices under this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> must submit monitoring plan under §63.8(f) and meet plan requirements; no -> must monitor the specified parameters
gates.quote: For scrubber control devices, you may request approval, in accordance with § 63.8(f), to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.9020(e).

gates.question: Can you meet the CMS data collection/operation requirements (operate CMS while process is operating and collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour)?
gates.test: yes -> alternative monitoring request must meet these CMS/data rules; no -> you may need to propose alternate data frequency and justify in plan
gates.quote: (1) You must operate your CMS and collect data at all times the process is operating. (2) You must collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour.

gates.question: Will you provide the information required in a request to monitor alternative parameters (description of affected source and parameters, demonstration methods, monitoring frequency, supporting calculations, averaging time)?
gates.test: yes -> submit request to Administrator per §63.8(f); no -> insufficient information for approval
gates.quote: A description of each affected source and the parameter(s) to be monitored to determine whether the affected source will continuously comply with the emission limitations and an explanation of the criteria used to select the parameter(s).

missing: Whether this facility is subject to Subpart NNNNN
Whether a continuous monitoring system (CMS) already exists for the bubbler or scrubber
Specific alternative parameters proposed (e.g., dipleg immersion depth, time between liquid changeouts) and supporting demonstration data
Whether you will submit a monitoring plan under §63.8(f) and the planned monitoring frequency/averaging times

candidates.title: Subpart QQQQQ

gates.question: Can you submit the required description of the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting that will be used to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations?
gates.test: yes -> you can request approval to use an alternative compliance/monitoring method; no -> you cannot obtain approval without this submission
gates.quote: You must submit a description of the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting that will be used and the proposed basis for demonstrating compliance.

missing: Whether the proposed alternative monitoring/testing has been previously performed and documented
The proposed monitoring plan content (test plan, monitoring procedures, frequency, QA/QC) and any prior test results to support the request
Whether you intend to begin using the alternative method only after Administrator approval (required)

candidates.title: Subpart SS

gates.question: Will you request Administrator approval to use alternatives to the monitoring requirements or procedures for control devices referenced by this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> Administrator may approve alternatives as provided in referencing subparts or paragraph (d); no -> standard monitoring provisions apply
gates.quote: (ii) The Administrator approves the use of alternatives to any monitoring requirements or procedures as provided in the referencing subpart or paragraph (d) of this section.

gates.question: Will you request approval to monitor a different parameter or set unique monitoring parameters instead of the parameters listed for CPMS/monitoring?
gates.test: yes -> you must request approval as specified and justify the alternative; no -> you must monitor the listed parameters and ranges
gates.quote: An owner or operator may request approval to monitor a different parameter than those established in paragraph (c)(6) of this section or to set unique monitoring parameters

missing: Which referencing subpart governs the specific control-device monitoring requirements for your source (to know where §63.996 alternatives would be invoked)
Demonstration that the alternative parameter (e.g., dipleg depth, changeout interval) correlates to control efficiency or established range for the control device
Whether you have submitted the parameter-range information in the Notification of Compliance Status or permit application as required by the referencing subpart

checklist.item: Confirm whether the facility is a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC
Confirm whether the HCl bubbler is a wet scrubber/scrubber control device (so scrubber-specific alternative monitoring rules apply)
Prepare and be ready to submit a monitoring plan per §63.8(f) describing the proposed alternative parameter(s), monitoring procedures, frequency, averaging time, and supporting calculations
Assemble performance test results or other data demonstrating the proposed alternative parameter correlates with control efficiency (baseline for established operating limits)

candidates.title: What are the requirements for monitoring and demonstrating continuous compliance?

gates.question: Do your enclosures vent to an add-on control device (for example, ducting from enclosures to an RTO) such that duct static pressure or flow rate monitoring would be required?
gates.test: yes -> This subpart requires installing a device to measure and record flow rate or duct static pressure; no -> this specific provision for enclosure-to-control-device monitoring is not applicable.
gates.quote: You must install a device to measure and record either the flow rate or the static pressure in the duct from each enclosure to the add-on control device.

gates.question: Can you meet continuous parameter monitoring system data frequency and availability requirements (CMS completes a cycle at least every 15 minutes and provides valid data for at least 90% of operating hours)?
gates.test: yes -> you can meet the continuous monitoring requirements and use averaged data per this subpart; no -> you would need to propose alternative monitoring or address data gaps.
gates.quote: The continuous parameter monitoring system must complete a minimum of one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period. You must have a minimum of four successive cycles of operation to have a valid hour of data.

missing: Whether your facility is an affected source under Subpart VVVV (subject applicability not included in provided text)
Whether each enclosure in question is routed to the regenerative thermal oxidizer (RTO) as the 'add-on control device'
Results of any performance test (Method 2 or other) establishing operating limits for flow or static pressure for each enclosure
Whether the enclosures are permanent total enclosures (PTE) as defined in Method 204, and any Table 4 operating limits referenced

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements

gates.question: Do you propose to use a static pressure measurement device installed in the duct immediately downstream of the hood exit (daily averaged readings) instead of measuring face velocity through natural-draft openings?
gates.test: yes -> the subpart describes installing a static pressure device with daily readings maintained relative to Method 2 performance test averages; no -> follow the default annual Methods 1 and 2 or other indicated procedures.
gates.quote: readings are recorded daily and maintained at 90 percent or better of the average vacuum recorded during the most recent Method 2 performance test series;

gates.question: Do you have a Method 1/2 performance test or PTE verification (Method 204) that establishes the baseline averages against which daily static-pressure readings will be maintained?
gates.test: yes -> you may use the alternate (once every 5 years) approach tied to the Method 2 baseline; no -> you must conduct the required Method 1/2 or Method 204 test or use annual measurements as specified.
gates.quote: Conduct annual flow rate measurements using EPA Methods 1 and 2 in appendix A to 40 CFR part 60, or conduct annual verification of a permanent total enclosure using EPA Method 204;

missing: Whether the specific affected sources/emission units at the facility fall under Subpart RRR applicability (the provided text does not state facility applicability)
Whether the baseline Method 2 or Method 204 test has been performed for the enclosures proposed for static pressure monitoring
Location details showing the duct point 'immediately downstream of the hood exit' where the static pressure sensor would be installed
Delegation status: whether the Administrator or the State permitting authority reviews alternate monitoring approvals for these sources

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements

gates.question: Will you submit an application to the Administrator for approval of alternate monitoring requirements (to replace face-velocity/Natural opening monitoring with duct static-pressure monitoring)?
gates.test: yes -> you must continue using the original monitoring requirement until approval is received; no -> you must keep current monitoring or follow other subpart procedures.
gates.quote: If the application to use an alternate monitoring requirement is approved, you must continue to use the original monitoring requirement until approval is received to use another monitoring requirement.

gates.question: Can you submit the alternate monitoring application by the notification of performance test (or no later than the notification of performance test)?
gates.test: yes -> your application will be considered per the timelines and content requirements; no -> you risk disapproval or must continue required monitoring until timely application is submitted.

Confirm whether the process fluids or heat exchange system are in ethylene oxide service (≥0.1% EO), which changes repair timing and sampling requirements.

If seeking to replace required grab sampling with composite sampling, prepare justification and identify whether the method provides equivalent sensitivity (10 ppm requirement for cooling water per §63.104(b)(3)) and whether Administrator approval will be requested under §63.114(c) / §63.151(f) or §63.152(e).

candidates.title: Primary Aluminum Reduction Plants

gates.question: Is your facility a primary aluminum reduction plant (subject to Subpart LL)?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart LL may apply; no -> Subpart LL does not apply
gates.quote: The owner operator of a primary aluminum reduction plant must comply with the requirements of this subpart by the applicable compliance date

gates.question: Does your facility have a pitch storage tank that is subject to the pitch storage tank POM limit provisions of § 63.843(d)?
gates.test: yes -> pitch storage tank POM limits apply; no -> those pitch-tank provisions do not apply
gates.quote: October 16, 2017 for ... the pitch storage tank POM limit provisions of § 63.843(d) which became effective October 15, 2015.

gates.question: Is the pitch storage tank required to be equipped with an emission control system that reduces inlet POM emissions by 95 percent or greater?
gates.test: yes -> control-device installation is required to meet 95% reduction; no -> different requirements may apply
gates.quote: Each pitch storage tank shall be equipped with an emission control system designed and operated to reduce inlet emissions of POM by 95 percent or greater.

gates.question: Is the control device for the pitch storage tank a carbon adsorber (i.e., will your compliance rely on a carbon adsorption system)?
gates.test: yes -> design-evaluation and monitoring items for carbon adsorbers apply; no -> other design-evaluation criteria apply
gates.quote: For carbon adsorbers, the design evaluation shall include the affinity of the organic vapors for carbon, the amount of carbon in each bed, the number of beds, the humidity of the feed gases

gates.question: Was the pitch storage tank shut down at the time the compliance date would have otherwise been required and subsequently restarted?
gates.test: yes -> special startup timing provisions for restarted sources apply; no -> standard compliance timing applies
gates.quote: By the 30th day following startup for a pitch storage tank. The 30-day period starts when the tank is first used to store pitch.

gates.question: Are you requesting additional time to install controls to meet the October 16, 2017 compliance date for the pitch storage tank?
gates.test: yes -> consider §63.6(i) extension procedures; no -> proceed with on-time compliance actions
gates.quote: may request that the Administrator ... grant an extension allowing the source up to 1 additional year to comply with the standard, if such additional period is necessary for the installation of controls.

gates.question: Was your extension request submitted in writing no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date?
gates.test: yes -> request meets the 120-day submittal timing; no -> see allowance for late submittal if need arose after deadline
gates.quote: must be submitted in writing to the appropriate authority no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date

gates.question: If the request was submitted after the 120-day deadline, did the need for the compliance extension arise after that deadline and before the compliance date due to circumstances beyond your reasonable control?
gates.test: yes -> late submittal may still be accepted under §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C); no -> late request may be untimely
gates.quote: provided the need for the compliance extension arose after that date, and the need arose due to circumstances beyond reasonable control of the owner or operator.

missing: Whether the facility is (in fact) a primary aluminum reduction plant subject to Subpart LL (not provided in the cited regulatory text).
Whether the specific pitch storage tank at issue is within the regulated source and subject to §63.843(d) (owner/operator must confirm applicability).
The actual date the pitch storage tank was restarted (to determine whether restart/startup timing provisions apply).
Whether an extension request has already been submitted, and if so the submission date and recipient (EPA vs. State permitting authority).
Whether the need for additional time (the 60-day request) arose after the 120-day submission deadline and whether the circumstances were beyond the owner's reasonable control.
Whether the State of Indiana is the permitting authority for granting extensions (i.e., whether State has an approved part 70 permit program or delegated authority).
Whether the source is subject to Title V permitting (affects incorporation of extension terms into a Title V permit if granted).
Any supporting documentation (compliance schedule, control description, milestones) required by §63.6(i)(6)(i) to accompany an extension request.

candidates.title: General Provisions

gates.question: Is the owner/operator requesting an extension of compliance (up to 1 additional year) because additional time is necessary for installation of controls?
gates.test: yes -> §63.6(i)(4)(i)(A) authorizes up to 1-year extension for installation of controls; no -> §63.6(i) extension may not apply
gates.quote: may request that the Administrator ... grant an extension allowing the source up to 1 additional year to comply with the standard, if such additional period is necessary for the installation of controls.

gates.question: Was the extension request submitted in writing at least 120 days prior to the compliance date (unless the late-submittal exception applies)?
gates.test: yes -> meets the §63.6(i)(4)(i)(B) presubmission timing; no -> check late-submittal exception in §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C)
gates.quote: Any request under this paragraph for an extension of compliance with a relevant standard must be submitted in writing to the appropriate authority no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date

gates.question: If the request was submitted after the 120-day deadline, did the need arise after that date and before the compliance date due to circumstances beyond reasonable control?
gates.test: yes -> late request may still stay applicability and be considered; no -> request likely untimely per §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C)
gates.quote: provided the need for the compliance extension arose after that date, and the need arose due to circumstances beyond reasonable control of the owner or operator.

missing: Whether an extension request has been submitted (and the exact submission date).
Documentation showing the need for additional time and whether that need arose after the 120-day deadline (if request was late).
Whether the request is nonfrivolous (requests that are nonfrivolous stay applicability while under consideration).
Whether the owner/operator has prepared the compliance schedule and control installation details required under §63.6(i)(6)(i) to support the extension request.
Which authority will review the extension (EPA Administrator versus Indiana state permitting authority) and whether the State has the delegated authority to grant the extension.

checklist.item: Confirm the facility is a primary aluminum reduction plant subject to Subpart LL.
Confirm the specific pitch storage tank is subject to the §63.843(d) 95% POM control requirement.
Confirm whether the pitch storage tank was shut down at the time compliance would otherwise have been required and the date it was restarted.
Confirm whether the planned control is a carbon adsorber and whether design-evaluation documentation addresses the carbon-adsorber items listed in §63.847(g)(2)(v).
Confirm whether an extension request has already been submitted and, if so, the submission date and to which authority.
If the request was submitted late, document whether the need for the extension arose after the 120-day deadline and before Oct 16, 2017 due to circumstances beyond reasonable control.
